apps.name: FastFlow Anomaly Detector
apps.summary: Flags surface defects on parts in one RTSP stream with an anomaly model trained on good parts only, and sends Insight the video with a defect heatmap drawn on it.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Flags surface defects on parts in one RTSP stream with an anomaly model trained on good parts only, and sends Insight the video with a defect heatmap drawn on it.

The decoded frame leaves the graph together with its anomaly map, so the application can paint the heatmap onto the pixels it came from and send the finished picture to Insight as H.264 video. Setting `output.save_dir` writes the same annotated frames as JPEGs.

```
RTSP decode (NV12) --> branch --> frame ------------+
                            \--> model (CVU preprocess + MLA FastFlow) --> anomaly map
                                                    |
    frame + map --> heatmap, boxes and verdict drawn on the frame --> video_sender
                                                        (H264 RTP/UDP -> Insight)
```

FastFlow returns a 256x256 map with the probability that each pixel does not belong to a good part. Connected regions at or above `inference.threshold` that cover at least `inference.min_region_px` map pixels are the defects; smaller ones are the speckle a good part produces. The heatmap covers only those regions, each gets a box, and a banner carries the verdict, the highest probability in the frame and the live frame rate. A good part therefore shows the plain picture with a green `OK`.

A FastFlow package knows one product. The packaged model knows the blue discs of the sample clip; for your own product, train with anomalib and plug the compiled package in, see [Use Your Own Model](#use-your-own-model).

sections.markdown: ![FastFlow anomaly detector preview](./example-assets/anomaly-detection/fastflow-anomaly-detector/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- `sima-cli` ([documentation](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/sima-cli/)) on the Modalix DevKit, or in a Neat SDK container paired with it.
- An RTSP H.264 source with a square picture and an [Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) URL reachable from the target. Insight can host the sample clip `assets/datasets/blue-discs/discs_demo.mp4`.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install on the Modalix DevKit, or under `/workspace` in a Neat SDK container paired with it. Only the example itself must run on the DevKit. If the Core and Insight selected by Apps are already installed, run the install as `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES=1 sima-cli neat install apps` to skip reinstalling them. See [Install Apps](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/README.md#install-apps).

Install the latest Neat Apps runtime and enter the installed bundle:

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/anomaly-detection/fastflow-anomaly-detector
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
| Model package | Role | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fastflow_demo_mpk.tar.gz` | Default | Direct artifact (Model Zoo `fastflow_demo`) |
| `<your-model>_mpk.tar.gz` | Supported | Compiled from an anomalib FastFlow export, see [Use Your Own Model](#use-your-own-model) |

Model packages come from the Model Zoo release below, which can differ from the installed platform version. Model Zoo downloads need your SiMa Developer Portal login: run `sima-cli login` once, or follow the device-login prompt the first download prints.

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/fastflow_demo_mpk.tar.gz"
cd ..
```

Set `model.path` in the config to the downloaded package.

sections.title: Prepare Insight
sections.markdown:
[Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) can host the input stream and show the annotated video. Upload `assets/datasets/blue-discs/discs_demo.mp4` under *RTSP Source* in the Insight Web UI, or use a clip of your own parts.

In the Insight Web UI, start the stream and copy its source URL. From a board, replace the container port shown in the URL with the published host port that `neat --json` reports.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`. Set `model.path`, `source.rtsp_url` and `output.insight.host`. If Insight uses a nondefault video port, set `output.insight.video_port` to the port reported by `neat --json`.

`output.heat_max` and `output.alpha` control the overlay: the first is the probability drawn at full colour, the second the opacity over the frame.

The stream must carry a square picture: the model input is square and its preprocess letterboxes anything else, which flattens the map. Keep `inference.frames` at `0` to run until you stop the application.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
### C++

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/fastflow-anomaly-detector \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

### Python

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
Both applications print one line when the pipeline is up, then run silently:

```
rtsp=rtsp://<insight-host-ip>:8554/src1 stream=720x720@30 map=256x256 threshold=0.5 min_region_px=300 insight=<insight-host-ip> video=9000 channel=0
```

Open the Insight Video Viewer for channel 0. The sample clip alternates defective and good discs, so the heatmap and the red `ANOMALY` banner appear and disappear every few discs. Stop with Ctrl-C; the application prints a summary:

```
processed=1080 flagged=590 video_sender=<insight-host-ip>:9000
```

Set `runtime.profile` to `true` for a rolling frame-rate line. Both applications keep up with a 720x720 stream at 30 fps on a Modalix.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- Verify stream reachability if the first frame times out. From a board, use the published host port instead of the container port.
- Verify the Insight host and video port if no video arrives.
- Verify `model.normalize` and the stream aspect ratio if defective parts show no heatmap: a wrong normalisation or a letterboxed frame flattens the map.
- Raise `inference.min_region_px` if good parts are flagged.

sections.title: Use Your Own Model
sections.markdown:
**1. Train and export with anomalib 2.6.** Install anomalib 2.6.2 in a Python environment of its own:

```bash
pip install anomalib==2.6.2
anomalib install
```

From 2.7.0 on, anomalib exports ONNX only through `torch.export`, which writes a different graph at opset 18 that `compile_model.py` does not handle. A model already trained with 2.7.0 needs no retraining: export its checkpoint with 2.6.2.

Train FastFlow on square photos of good parts with [anomalib](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/anomalib), using its `Fastflow` model and `Folder` dataset. Set `flow_steps: 4` and `conv3x3_only: true` in the model config: anomalib's default of 8 steps loses pixel accuracy in bfloat16 on the MLA, 4 steps keep it. Export at 256x256:

```bash
anomalib export --model Fastflow --ckpt_path model.ckpt --export_type onnx --input_size "[256, 256]"
```

**2. Compile.** On the development host, in the Model Compiler environment, from a clone of this repository (the compile helper is not part of the installed bundle):

```bash
activate-model-compiler
python3 examples/anomaly-detection/fastflow-anomaly-detector/scripts/compile_model.py \
  --model model.onnx --calib-images /data/my_product/train/good
```

The script converts the network to bfloat16 and writes `build/model/model_mpk.tar.gz`. It patches two constructs in anomalib's export that the Model Compiler mishandles, the per-image LayerNorm and the 5-D map average; without the patches the package produces noise or does not load. There is no INT8: FastFlow's coupling blocks amplify 8-bit error until the map saturates on every image.

`--calib-images` needs photographs of real good parts even though bfloat16 fits no quantisation scales. Compiled from a synthetic input instead, the same export scores image AUROC 0.50 with the map saturated on every image, against 0.99 with the photographs.

**3. Plug in.** Copy the package to `models/` and change three keys in `config.yaml` together:

```yaml
model:
  path: models/model_mpk.tar.gz
  normalize:                 # anomalib packages normalise inside the graph, so zeros and ones;
    mean: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]    # the demo package needs its blue-disc mean instead
    stddev: [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
inference:
  min_region_px: 1000        # smallest region that counts as a defect; per product
```

For `min_region_px`, run the application on good parts and raise the value until the summary reports `flagged=0`, then check that defective parts are still flagged. Measured on MVTec AD bottle on a Modalix, the 4-step model keeps image AUROC 0.99 and pixel AUROC 0.97, and a package runs at about 7 ms per inference.

apps.name: PatchCore Anomaly Detector
apps.summary: Detects visual anomalies in industrial images or video using a compiled WideResNet-50 patch-feature extractor and a host-side coreset memory bank calibrated from your own known-good images.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Detects visual anomalies in industrial images or video using a compiled WideResNet-50 patch-feature extractor and a host-side coreset memory bank calibrated from your own known-good images.

PatchCore learns only what normal looks like. The MLA turns every frame into a 28x28 grid of patch descriptions (1,536 values each, from `wide_resnet50_2` with torchvision `IMAGENET1K_V1` weights). `--calibrate` keeps a small, diverse set of descriptions from your known-good images as the memory bank. At run time each patch is compared with its nearest bank entry on the host: patches far from everything normal are highlighted, and the worst patch decides the frame's `normal` / `ANOMALOUS` verdict.

```
image_dir / video_file:  decode on host --> letterbox to 224x224 --> model (MLA) --> patch descriptions
rtsp:                    RTSP decode --> branch --> model (CVU preprocess + MLA) --> "embedding" --+
                                               \--> "frame" ----------------------------------------+--> joined per frame
patch descriptions + frame --> nearest bank entry per patch (host) --> verdict + heatmap --> Insight / saved overlays
```

The bank is built from the compiled model's own descriptions, not from a float PyTorch model: the compiled model's values differ slightly, and a bank from another model shifts every distance and weakens the separation between normal and defective. `bank_meta.json` records the model package's hash, so a bank built for a different package is rejected at load.

Skip this section if you only run the C++ variant. The Python variant runs in the `pyneat` Python environment that the Apps installer sets up with Neat Core (`~/pyneat` by default). Activate it in every new shell, install the example's Python dependencies once, and confirm `pyneat` imports:

Model Zoo downloads need your SiMa Developer Portal login: run `sima-cli login` once, or follow the device-login prompt the first download prints.

```bash
mkdir -p models
cd models
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"

cd ..
```

Set `model.path` in the example config to the downloaded package.

sections.title: Prepare the memory bank
sections.markdown:
Before scoring anything, build a memory bank from a directory of known-good ("nominal") images of your own inspection target. The bundled `assets/datasets/patchcore/` set exists only to make this demo reproducible without your own images, and is not a substitute for your own target's data:

- `nominal/` -- 16 real known-good reference images. `calibration.nominal_images_dir` points here by default; `--calibrate` below builds the memory bank from 13 of them and measures the threshold on the other 3.
- `held_out_normal/` -- 4 further real known-good images, deliberately excluded from calibration, used only by this example's own test suite to check that genuinely normal images the bank never saw still score below the threshold.
- `images/` -- an image-directory scoring input: one normal-looking image (`plain_0.png`) and four images with synthetic scratch defects (`scratch_0.png`-`scratch_3.png`), for exercising `source.type: image_dir` end to end.

To calibrate against your own inspection target instead, point `calibration.nominal_images_dir` at a directory of your own known-good images (a few dozen is a reasonable starting point) before running `--calibrate`. Capture them with the same camera, framing, and lighting you will run with.

The model input is 224x224. Every image, video frame, and RTSP frame is letterboxed into it the same way: scaled to fit with its aspect ratio kept, and centered between gray bars. The whole frame is inspected, but a wide frame gets fewer model pixels than a square one (a 16:9 frame fills 224x126), so keep the part large in the frame. Calibrate with images from the same camera and resolution you will run with.

`--calibrate` keeps every 5th nominal image out of the bank and measures the threshold on those, so the threshold reflects images the bank has not memorized. Set `calibration.threshold_images_dir` to use a separate set instead.

`calibration.coreset_ratio` sets how many nominal patches the bank keeps. The default 0.0004 keeps 4 of the 10,192 patches from the demo's 13 bank images, which is enough for its uniform texture and keeps scoring fast. On a busy or varied scene a bank this small matches normal clutter poorly, which raises the threshold until real defects can go unflagged; raise the ratio (the PatchCore paper keeps 1-10%) and check that a known defect is caught. Scoring cost grows with the bank: measured on a Modalix DevKit (Platform 3.0), host scoring takes about 1-2 ms, 30 ms, and 400 ms per frame for 5, 125, and 1,254 vectors (C++ and Python are similar).

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/patchcore-anomaly-detector --calibrate --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

or, with the Python variant (after [Set Up Python](#set-up-python)):

```bash
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py --calibrate --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

Both write `memory_bank.path` / `memory_bank.meta_path` from `calibration.nominal_images_dir`, and share the same on-disk format -- a bank built with one binary loads and scores in the other. Re-run `--calibrate` whenever `model.path` changes, the inspection target or camera changes, or you change any `calibration` setting.

sections.title: Prepare Insight
sections.markdown:
`video_file` and `rtsp` send the annotated video to Insight. Insight installs with the Apps runtime; start it on the board and leave it running:

```bash
source ~/.simaai/neat-insight/venv/bin/activate && neat-insight
```

The first start installs `mkcert` with `sudo apt-get`, so run it from an interactive shell and enter the board password when asked. Open `https://<board-ip>:9900` in a browser and accept the self-signed certificate. When Insight runs on the board, set `output.insight.host` to `127.0.0.1`.

For `rtsp`, Insight can also provide the stream: under *RTSP Source*, upload a clip (for example `assets/datasets/patchcore/video/test.mp4`) or select a webcam, start it, and copy its URL (for example `rtsp://<board-ip>:8554/src1`) into `source.rtsp.url`.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown: Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`. Set `model.path`, `source.type` and its matching source fields, `memory_bank.path` / `memory_bank.meta_path`, and `calibration.nominal_images_dir` before the first `--calibrate` run. The shipped config uses `source.type: video_file` with the bundled clip. For `source.type: video_file` or `rtsp`, also set `output.insight.host` to the machine running Insight. For `source.type: rtsp` with `codec: h265` or `mjpeg`, also set `source.rtsp.width`/`height` (see Troubleshooting).

sections.markdown:
### C++

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/patchcore-anomaly-detector \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

### Python

After [Set Up Python](#set-up-python):

```bash
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
Every processed image or frame prints its score, the calibrated threshold, and the verdict. Only regions scoring above the calibrated patch threshold are highlighted (yellow to red); normal regions are left unchanged.

With the shipped config (`video_file`, the bundled clip), the app plays the clip once and streams it to Insight. In the Insight video viewer (channel 0), the first 60 frames show plain texture with no highlight and `verdict=normal`; from frame 61 the scratches and colored dots are highlighted and every frame is `ANOMALOUS`:

```
frame=1: score=17.0073 threshold=20.5151 verdict=normal (mla=...ms host=...ms)
...
frame=61: score=35.3749 threshold=20.5151 verdict=ANOMALOUS (mla=...ms host=...ms)
...
Done: 450 frames processed  video_sender=127.0.0.1:9000
```

With `source.type: image_dir` and the bundled `images/`, overlays are written to `output.dir`:

```
assets/datasets/patchcore/images/plain_0.png: score=16.8013 threshold=20.5151 verdict=normal (mla=2022.1ms host=7.9ms)
assets/datasets/patchcore/images/scratch_0.png: score=34.6679 threshold=20.5151 verdict=ANOMALOUS (mla=32.3ms host=18.1ms)
...
Done: 5 images processed -- overlays written to sandbox/patchcore-anomaly-detector
```

For `video_file` and `rtsp`, each frame's verdict is also sent to Insight as `classification` metadata on `output.insight.metadata_port` (default 9100): Insight draws it as a label on the video (for example `ANOMALOUS score=34.7 thr=20.5`), and `data.anomaly` carries the raw `score`, `threshold`, and `verdict` for other consumers.

`mla` is the model time per image (the first one includes setup); `host` is the nearest-neighbor scoring and overlay drawing. In `rtsp` mode the model runs inside the graph, so `mla` there is the wait for the next frame. `video_file` and `rtsp` save every Nth overlay frame to `output.dir` only when `output.save_every` is above 0 (off by default; saving has no limit, so keep N large on long runs).

Measured on a Modalix DevKit (Platform 3.0, build 2121), RTSP at 30 fps with the default bank:

| Stream | C++ | Python |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 224x224 | about 26 fps | about 25 fps |
| 720x720 | about 15 fps | about 18 fps |

At larger frames, drawing the full-size heatmap takes most of the host time. When scoring is slower than the stream, the app drops older frames instead of queueing them, so the Insight view stays within about a second of the camera. A larger `calibration.coreset_ratio` lowers the frame rate only slightly (about 3 fps less at a bank of about 100 vectors).

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pyneat'`: activate the `pyneat` environment (see [Set Up Python](#set-up-python)).
- `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'`: install the example's dependencies with `pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt` (see [Set Up Python](#set-up-python)).
- `memory bank not found`: run `--calibrate` first.
- `memory bank was built against a different model package`: `model.path` changed since the last `--calibrate`; rebuild the bank.
- `bank_meta.json is missing patch_threshold`: rerun `--calibrate` to regenerate the bank.
- Confirm `source.image_dir` / `source.video_path` / `source.rtsp.url` matches the configured `source.type`.
- `rtsp`: `failed to resolve source geometry` -- the stream wasn't reachable, or (for `codec: h265`/`mjpeg`) didn't expose probeable width/height; set `source.rtsp.width`/`height` explicitly.
- Nothing appears in Insight: confirm Insight is running (see [Prepare Insight](#prepare-insight)), `output.insight.host` is reachable, and Insight is listening on the configured `video_port`/`channel`.
- Every frame of a new camera is `ANOMALOUS`: calibrate on known-good images from that camera, at the resolution and framing you run with.
- `--calibrate` looks stalled on a large nominal set: it prints progress every 10 images; lowering `calibration.coreset_ratio` reduces both build time and per-frame scoring cost.

sections.title: Known limitations
sections.markdown:
- MVTec AD is not vendored into this repo or used for the shipped memory bank (its license is non-commercial research use); build your own bank from a nominal set captured on your own target.

apps.name: MIPI Camera Capture
apps.summary: Captures NV12 frames from a MIPI camera and saves selected frames with timing and luminance diagnostics. It uses Neat CameraInput with a zero-copy DMA-BUF path.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Captures NV12 frames from a MIPI camera and saves selected frames with timing and luminance diagnostics. It uses Neat CameraInput with a zero-copy DMA-BUF path.

The camera-to-Neat path remains zero-copy. Copying occurs only for the explicitly selected snapshots written by the Python application.

Install on the Modalix DevKit, or under `/workspace` in a Neat SDK container paired with it. Only the example itself must run on the DevKit. See [Install Apps](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/README.md#install-apps).

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/benchmarking/mipi-camera-capture
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown: This camera capture example does not use a model. No model download or compilation is required.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`. Set `camera.name` to a name reported by `cam -l`, or leave it empty to use the default camera. Change the capture duration, sample times, or output directory if needed.

Keep `camera.strict_zero_copy` enabled to report an error instead of silently copying frames when zero-copy capture is unavailable.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

The output directory contains sampled NV12 frames and `summary.json`. A Modalix
DevKit does not ship `ffmpeg`, so copy a frame to a workstation with FFmpeg
installed and convert it there for visual inspection:

On the target, pick a frame and copy it out. Set `OUT_DIR` to the
`output.directory` from your config; the command below uses the shipped default.
The exact filename includes the observed capture time, so take the one the
application printed:

```bash
OUT_DIR="sandbox/mipi-camera-capture"
FRAME="$(realpath "$(find "${OUT_DIR}" -name 'frame_00_*.nv12' -print -quit)")"
echo "${FRAME}"
```

From the workstation, copy that file over and convert it there. A raw NV12 file
carries no dimensions, so `-video_size` must match the `camera.width` and
`camera.height` you configured. At any other size the conversion produces a
skewed or garbled image instead of failing:

```bash
scp <user>@<target>:<path-printed-above> ./frame.nv12
ffmpeg -f rawvideo -pixel_format nv12 -video_size 1920x1080 \
  -i frame.nv12 \
  -frames:v 1 frame.png
```

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown: The application prints `CAPTURE` records for the requested sample times and one final `SUMMARY` record. A healthy run reports frames, zero timeouts, `error: null`, and stable luminance percentiles.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- If camera discovery fails, confirm that `cam -l` reports the configured name.
- If strict allocation negotiation fails, confirm that the installed Neat Library, libcamera plugin, and pipeline handler were built from compatible releases.
- If the requested format is adjusted or rejected, select a resolution, frame rate, and NV12 layout supported by the sensor and ISP.
- Set `strict_zero_copy: false` only when a diagnostic run may use Neat's explicit CPU-copy fallback.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Runs a selected detection, pose, segmentation, classification, or depth model on a strict zero-copy MIPI camera. Detection and segmentation can also stream video and metadata to Insight.

The application loads one profile per process, keeping MLA memory use predictable while making each task independently testable.

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![MIPI multi-model preview](./example-assets/benchmarking/mipi-multi-model/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- `sima-cli` ([documentation](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/sima-cli/)) on a supported Modalix or DevKit target.
- A MIPI camera supported by the installed kernel, libcamera pipeline, and IPA configuration.
- A Neat Library release whose camera bridge forwards the camera's own DMA-BUFs (Platform 3.0).

Confirm that libcamera sees the camera:

```bash
cam -l
```

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install the latest Neat Apps runtime and enter the installed bundle:

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/benchmarking/mipi-multi-model
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
The default profile uses YOLO26n detection. Every profile consumes a compiled `.tar.gz` package directly.

| Profile | Task | Model package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `detect` | YOLO26n detection | `yolo26n-det-int8-b1.tar.gz` |
| `pose` | YOLO26n pose | `yolo26n-pose-bf16-mla_tess-b1.tar.gz` |
| `segment` | YOLO26n instance segmentation | `yolo26n-seg-bf16-mla_tess.tar.gz` |
| `ssd` | SSD-MobileNet V2 detection | `ssd_mobilenet_v2_modalix_int8_tess_mla_mpk.tar.gz` |
| `classify` | ResNet-50 classification | `resnet_50_mpk.tar.gz` |
| `depth` | MiDaS v2.1 Small depth | `midas_v21_small_256_mpk.tar.gz` |

Model packages come from the Model Zoo release below, which can differ from the installed platform version. Download the packages for the profiles you plan to run into `models/`:

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo26-detection/yolo26n-det-int8-b1.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo26-pose/yolo26n-pose-bf16-mla_tess-b1.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo26-segmentation/yolo26n-seg-bf16-mla_tess.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/resnet_50_mpk.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/midas_v21_small_256_mpk.tar.gz"
sima-cli download \
  "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/ssd_mobilenet_v2_modalix_int8_tess_mla_mpk.tar.gz"
cd ..
```

Each profile reads `models/<model package>` by default.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`. Change only `model.profile`; set `model.path` only when using a package outside `models/`. `runtime.frames` controls how many results are pulled. Set `insight.host` to stream detection or segmentation to Insight; `insight.video_port`, `insight.metadata_port`, `insight.channel`, and `insight.bitrate_kbps` select the destination. Each setting has a command-line override, such as `--insight-host`.

The camera path captures 1920x1080 NV12 at 30 FPS. Neat owns MPK parsing, model compatibility, decoding, and the EV74 preprocessing/postprocessing stages.

The graph ends with a manually added, named output so the composition is explicit:

```python
camera_graph.add(pyneat.nodes.camera_input(camera_options))
model_graph = model.graph(route)
model_graph.add(pyneat.nodes.output("results"))
```

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
List the available profiles:

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py --list-profiles
```

Run the configured profile, or select one on the command line:

```bash
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml \
  --describe

python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml \
  --profile pose
```

Stream YOLO26 detection or segmentation to Insight, using the `insight` settings from the configuration or these overrides:

```bash
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --profile segment \
  --model models/yolo26n-seg-bf16-mla_tess.tar.gz \
  --continuous \
  --insight-host 192.168.1.127 \
  --insight-video-port 9000 \
  --insight-metadata-port 9100 \
  --insight-channel 0
```

The Insight graph uses `RealtimeLatestByStream` independently for the model and video branches, preventing either consumer from building a stale camera-frame backlog. Segmentation metadata includes per-instance polygons, class labels, confidence, and bounding boxes.

The application rejects the graph before execution, with or without Insight, unless Neat's camera
bridge refuses CPU copies. At run time the bridge forwards each camera frame's DMA-BUF to the
model without copying and stops the pipeline on any frame that would need a copy.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
Each frame prints the selected profile and a task-specific summary, followed by a `PASS` line. For example:

```text
frame=0 profile=detect detections=6
PASS strict-zero-copy MIPI -> YOLO26n object detection -> results
```

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- If camera discovery fails, confirm that `cam -l` reports a camera and that the correct overlay is installed.
- If model loading fails, confirm the file is a compiled `.tar.gz` model package compatible with the installed Neat runtime. Neat owns package parsing and compatibility validation.
- If the pipeline stops with `Camera buffer is not one forwardable DMA-BUF and copying is disabled`, the camera delivered a frame that is not one DMA-BUF. Use the platform `libcamera` package, which delivers each frame as one DMA-BUF.
- Run with `--validate-model-only` to inspect the package without loading Neat or opening the camera.

apps.name: Model Benchmark
apps.summary: Measures latency, throughput, power, and energy for any compiled model package, then saves the results as JSON.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Measures latency, throughput, power, and energy for any compiled model package, then saves the results as JSON.

This synthetic model benchmark does not measure input decoding, Insight output, overlays, or application postprocessing.

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![Model benchmark preview](./example-assets/benchmarking/model-benchmark/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- `sima-cli` ([documentation](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/sima-cli/)) on the Modalix DevKit, or in a Neat SDK container paired with it.
- A compiled model package supported by `pyneat.Model`.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install on the Modalix DevKit, or under `/workspace` in a Neat SDK container paired with it. Only the example itself must run on the DevKit. If the Core and Insight selected by Apps are already installed, run the install as `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES=1 sima-cli neat install apps` to skip reinstalling them. See [Install Apps](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/README.md#install-apps).

Install the latest Neat Apps runtime and enter the installed bundle:

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/benchmarking/model-benchmark
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
Use any compatible compiled MPK. Apps CI exercises the benchmark with `yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz`; it is not a required default.

Model packages come from the Model Zoo release below, which can differ from the installed platform version. Replace `<model-file>` with the package to benchmark:

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/<model-file>"
cd ..
```

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown: Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml` and set `model.path`. You can also change the minimum frames and duration of each benchmark pass and the JSON report path, or pass those values on the command line.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --model models/<model-file>.tar.gz \
  --frames 100 \
  --min-duration-ms 30000 \
  --output-json sandbox/model-benchmark/report.json
```

The command prints headline metrics and writes the complete report to the selected JSON path.

The benchmark runs a latency pass and a throughput pass. Each pass continues until it has measured at least `--frames` samples and run for at least `--min-duration-ms` milliseconds (30000 by default, `benchmark.min_duration_ms` in the config). Pass `--min-duration-ms 0` for a quick check that stops after `--frames` samples.

Without `--decode-type`, the model runs through the route its package declares. Add `--decode-type yolo26-det` or `--decode-type yolo26-seg` to benchmark a YOLO26 package through its BoxDecode route instead. Every report records the requested decode type and the postprocess Core resolved, so the two routes stay distinguishable.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.markdown: See the maintained [benchmark results](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/examples/benchmarking/model-benchmark/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md) for measurements from Apps-supported packages.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
The application prints headline metrics and the path it wrote the full report to:

```text
latency_ms=6.520167780941697
latency_p99_ms=7.116750399999998
fps=334.74326851174976
avg_power_watts=14.64375
energy_joules=4.374621203020843
report_json=sandbox/model-benchmark/report.json
```

The `report_json=` line names where the full report was written; trust it rather
than either setting, because `--output-json` takes precedence over
`output.report_json` and the documented run above passes that flag.

These numbers depend on the model package and the board, so treat them as an
example of the shape rather than a target; compare your own against the
maintained benchmark results linked in the `Benchmark Results` section above.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- Activate `~/pyneat` if the `pyneat` module is unavailable.
- Confirm the model path points to a compiled `.tar.gz` package.
- A zero power result means board power telemetry was unavailable; the model benchmark still completed.
- If results fall well below the maintained table, check the MLA clock with `cat /sys/class/devfreq/5000000.mla/cur_freq`. The table was measured at 1000 MHz; a board that boots at 600 MHz measures about 40% lower FPS.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
| Model package |
| --- |
| `resnet_50_mpk.tar.gz` |
| `resnet_18_mpk.tar.gz` |
| `efficientnet_b0_mpk.tar.gz` |
| `densenet_121_mpk.tar.gz` |

Model packages come from the Model Zoo release below, which can differ from the installed platform version.

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/resnet_50_mpk.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/resnet_18_mpk.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/efficientnet_b0_mpk.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/densenet_121_mpk.tar.gz"
cd ..
```

Each model is its own profile in the config; add more supported classification models the same
way by adding another entry under `models`.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`:

- `models.<name>.path` — path to each downloaded model package.
- `io.input` — a single image path or a directory of images. The directory is read one level
  deep: files directly inside it are classified and subdirectories are ignored. Leave empty to
  classify the bundled sample goldfish image (downloads it on first run; needs network access).
- `io.output_dir` — dedicated directory where the selected reports and
  `thumbnails/` are written; each run replaces its previous contents.
- `io.output_format` — which reports to write: any of `html`, `json`, `csv`.
  Ships as `[html]`; `thumbnails/` is written only when `html` is selected.

Remove a `models` entry to run with fewer models, or add one to compare an additional model.
Profile names may contain letters, digits, `_` and `-` (they become config keys, report columns
and CSV/JSON fields). Each profile is fully self-contained:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Compiled model package. |
| `input_width` / `input_height` | Model input dimensions. |
| `preprocess` | Preprocessing preset. Only `imagenet` (standard ImageNet normalization) is implemented. |
| `output` | Output interpretation. Only `softmax` is implemented: the model produces raw per-class scores, softmax is applied, and index `i` maps to `label_map[i]`. |
| `num_classes` | Number of classes the model outputs. |
| `label_map` | Path to a text file with one label per line (line index = class id; blank lines within the first `num_classes` lines are rejected). Omit for numeric labels. |
| `top_k` | How many predictions to keep per image. |

`preprocess` and `output` exist so a future model that needs different normalization or output
handling can declare it explicitly instead of being silently misinterpreted; adding support for a
new value is a small, explicit code change in both `main.py` and `main.cpp`.

sections.markdown:
### C++

```bash

  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

### Python

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

sections.title: Understanding the Report
sections.markdown:
Each run writes to `io.output_dir` (default `sandbox/report/`). `io.output_format`
selects which of these are written; it ships as `[html]`, and the formats are
`html`, `json` and `csv`:

| File | Written when | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `report.html` | `html` | Browsable report: thumbnails, per-model predictions and confidence, agreement/disagreement, filtering, sorting. |
| `thumbnails/` | `html` | Small JPEG copies of each classified image, referenced by `report.html`. |
| `report.json` | `json` | Same results in machine-readable form: predictions, timing, per-class summary, skipped files. |
| `report.csv` | `csv` | Flat per-image, per-model rows: top-1 class, confidence, inference time, full top-k. |

The thumbnails follow `html` because nothing else references them; for 21 images
they were 288 KB of roughly 420 KB written, so a run that only needs `json`
writes considerably less. Request several formats with
`output_format: [html, json, csv]`.

Open `report.html` in a browser. It lists every classified image with a thumbnail and each
selected model's top predictions and confidence. Use the controls above the table to:

- Check or uncheck models to show or hide their columns and recompute agreement for just the
  models you pick.
- Filter by result (all / agreement / disagreement / errors), by predicted class (text search), or
  by a minimum confidence threshold.
- Sort by confidence, predicted class, or result.

Example report (4 models against a directory of images):

![Example image classification explorer report](./example-assets/classification/image-classification-explorer/report-example.png)

Files with an unsupported extension are listed under **Skipped files** and are not classified;
subdirectories of the input directory are not listed, since the scan is one level deep.
Files with a supported extension that cannot be decoded stay in the main table with a per-model
`error` cell (and, when `json` is selected, an `errors` entry in `report.json`);
neither case stops the run.

One run writes one report. Two runs publishing into the same `io.output_dir` at
the same time is not supported and is not detected: give each concurrent run its
own output directory. A run interrupted part-way through replacing the directory
costs the previous report; the next run writes a fresh one.

**How large a collection is practical.** The input directory is not capped, but
the report is one HTML page and every result is held in memory until it is
written, so the collection size that is useful is smaller than the one that
fits. Measured on a Modalix DevKit with the four models above, at about 288 ms
and 6 KB of report per image:

| Images | Run time | `report.json` | `report.html` |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 | ~5 min | 3 MB | 3 MB |
| 10,000 | ~48 min | 34 MB | 26 MB |
| 50,000 | ~4 h | 170 MB | 130 MB |
| 100,000 | ~8 h | 340 MB | 259 MB |

Past roughly 10,000 images `report.html` stops being practical to open and
browse, which is what the report is for, and a large enough collection can
exhaust memory and end the run with no report at all. Split bigger collections
across several runs, each with its own `io.output_dir`.

Each run replaces the previous contents of `io.output_dir` as a unit, so the directory is either
the complete previous report or the complete new one. Use an empty or dedicated directory: a run
only replaces a directory that carries the hidden `.image-classification-explorer-report` marker
from a previous run and holds nothing else; any other non-empty directory is refused.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
Both implementations write the same report, so the check is the same whichever
you ran: the run ends with a summary naming the report directory, and every
model agrees on the sample image.

```text
Done in 3292.5 ms. Report written to sandbox/report
  report.html, thumbnails/
```

The summary names the files that run actually wrote, so it follows
`io.output_format`: with the shipped `[html]` it lists `report.html` and
`thumbnails/`, and adding `json` or `csv` adds those.

With `io.input` left `null`, the bundled goldfish sample is classified by every
profile in `config.yaml`. Opening `report.html` should show class `1` winning
for each model. The same results read more compactly from `report.csv`, which
needs `csv` in `io.output_format`:

```text
image                     model            status  top1_class_id  top1_label  top1_probability
/tmp/sima_imagenet_...    resnet_50        ok      1              goldfish    0.9462
/tmp/sima_imagenet_...    resnet_18        ok      1              goldfish    0.9995
/tmp/sima_imagenet_...    efficientnet_b0  ok      1              goldfish    0.7786
/tmp/sima_imagenet_...    densenet_121     ok      1              goldfish    0.9586
```

Exact probabilities vary with the model package; what matters is that class `1`
wins for every profile and that `status` is `ok` rather than `error`. The two
implementations produce identical `report.csv`, `report.html` and thumbnail
names for the same input, once the separately measured per-image `inference_ms`
and total time are excluded. Those timings differ between any two runs by
design; anything else differing between the two implementations is a defect.

A per-image failure does not stop the run: the image keeps its row and the
failing model gets an `error` cell in the report and a line on stderr, so a
partial result is always visible rather than silently missing.

```text
  images/broken.jpg: resnet_50 failed: Failed to read image: images/broken.jpg
```

If `validation.expected_class_id` is set and the sample does not match it, the
run still writes its report and notes the mismatch on stderr rather than
failing:

```text
Note: resnet_50 top1=393 (0.4871) did not match expected_class_id=1
  (min_probability=0.2); see report for details.
```

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- Verify each `models.<name>.path` if a model fails to load.
- Set `io.input` to a readable local image or directory if downloading or decoding the fallback
  image fails.
Both entrypoints report failures the same way, so a script can branch on the
exit code regardless of the language it ran:

| Exit code | Meaning |
| ---: | --- |
| `0` | The run completed and the report was written. |
| `2` | The command line or `config.yaml` is wrong (`Invalid configuration: ...`). |
| `3` | The input could not be read: a missing path, an empty directory, or a failed fallback download. |
| `6` | A model or the report itself failed at runtime. |

A per-image, per-model inference failure does not fail the run: it is recorded
in the report and the exit code stays `0`.

- Check `report.json`'s `skipped` list and each image's `errors` object for files that failed to
  process (add `json` to `io.output_format`; `report.html` shows the same failures in its
  per-model cells). `errors` is keyed by model name, so one image can record a failure for one
  model while retaining predictions from the others.

The application prints one line per image and a final count. The C++ binary also
prints `[INFER]` and `[DEPTH]` diagnostic lines between them and quotes the
filenames; both are normal.

```text
[1/21] 000000081061.jpg -> 000000081061.png
...
Done: 21 images processed
```

visualization per input image. With the packaged `assets/datasets/coco` folder
that is 21 files. Each is a side-by-side image: the resized input on the left,
its depth colormap on the right. The colormap is normalized per image, so
brightness is relative within one image and not comparable between images.

apps.name: Parallel Apps in Docker
apps.summary: Runs six Neat applications side by side in Docker containers on one Modalix DevKit, each sending live video and results to its own Insight channel.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Runs six Neat applications side by side in Docker containers on one Modalix DevKit, each sending live video and results to its own Insight channel.

Each container runs one Apps example with its own config: instance segmentation, RF-DETR object detection, multi-class tracking, pose estimation, tiny-drone tracking, and BlazePose 3D pose estimation. You install the Apps bundle in the Neat SDK, pack each example into an ARM64 image, and push the images to the SDK's container registry. The DevKit pulls them from there. Each image holds only the example's binary, its `src/common` files, its config, and its model. Each container mounts the DevKit's installed Neat and system libraries read-only and gets the accelerator and video codec devices, so it behaves like a normal run of the same example. All six share the DevKit's machine learning accelerator (MLA).

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![Six Docker containers on six Insight channels](./example-assets/docker/parallel-apps/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- The Neat SDK set up with your Modalix DevKit (`sima-cli sdk setup --devkit`). This starts the SDK's container registry and the `dk` DevKit commands. Run every command below in the Neat SDK shell.
- The same Neat Core on the DevKit as in the installed Apps bundle. The containers run the DevKit's Neat with binaries built against the bundle's Core; the Install Apps step installs that Core on the DevKit.
- A Neat Core that admits Modalix in containers (Core develop `e1eddd4` or newer). Older Cores identify the board from `/proc/device-tree`, which Docker hides, and every application exits with `closed owned platform capability unavailable`.
- Docker on the DevKit. If it is missing, `dk container setup` installs it.
- Six H.264 RTSP sources: people for segmentation and both pose examples, traffic for detection and tracking, and drones for the drone tracker. [Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) can host them under RTSP Source from its video catalog, and the Apps bundle ships a drone clip at `assets/datasets/yolo26-tiny-drone-tracker/anti_uav_multi_uav_source_demo.mp4`.
- Insight with at least six channels, reachable from the DevKit. Running Insight on the DevKit itself is the most reliable choice: the applications then send to `127.0.0.1`. Insight inside the SDK publishes four channels by default (set up the SDK with `--insight-video-channels 8` for six), and on macOS Docker Desktop can fail to forward some of its UDP ports.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install under `/workspace` in the Neat SDK container paired with your DevKit; the images are built there and the containers run on the DevKit. If the Core and Insight selected by Apps are already installed, run the install as `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES=1 sima-cli neat install apps` to skip reinstalling them. See [Install Apps](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/README.md#install-apps).

```bash
cd /workspace
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/docker/parallel-apps
```

Run the remaining commands in the Neat SDK container, from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
Each container gets its own folder under `models/`, named after the container, and its image holds only that folder. Model packages come from the Model Zoo release below, which can differ from the installed platform version.

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
MODELS="https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix"
mkdir -p models/neat-segmentation models/neat-detection models/neat-tracking models/neat-pose models/neat-drone models/neat-blazepose
(cd models/neat-segmentation && sima-cli download "${MODELS}/yolo26-segmentation/yolo26m-seg-int8-b1.tar.gz")
(cd models/neat-detection && sima-cli download "${MODELS}/rf_detr_small_w8a8_w16a16_backbone_mpk.tar.gz" && sima-cli download "${MODELS}/rf_detr_small_w8a8_w16a16_decoder_mpk.tar.gz")
(cd models/neat-tracking && sima-cli download "${MODELS}/yolo26-detection/yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz")
(cd models/neat-pose && sima-cli download "${MODELS}/yolo26-pose/yolo26m-pose-int8-b1.tar.gz")
(cd models/neat-drone && sima-cli download "${MODELS}/yolo26n_p2_tiny_drone_int8_qat_b1_mpk.tar.gz")
(cd models/neat-blazepose && sima-cli download "${MODELS}/blazepose_ghum_heavy_w16a16_mpk.tar.gz")
cp models/neat-tracking/yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz models/neat-blazepose/
```

Six applications share one MLA, so this example uses the INT8 segmentation package instead of the BF16 one its own README defaults to.

Inside an image, the container's folder appears as `models/`, so a config names a model as `models/<file>`. To use another model, follow that example's README and place the file in the container's folder.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Each image holds its example's own `src/common/config.yaml`. Edit the six configs as their READMEs describe, with one difference: give each example its own Insight channel. Insight maps video port `9000 + N` and metadata port `9100 + N` to channel `N`, and all six configs start on channel 0.

| Container | Example config | Model | RTSP source | Insight ports |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `neat-segmentation` | `examples/segmentation/single-stream-instance-segmenter` | `model.path: models/yolo26m-seg-int8-b1.tar.gz` | `source.rtsp.url` | `output.insight.video_port: 9000`, `metadata_port: 9100` |
| `neat-detection` | `examples/object-detection/rfdetr-detection-segmentation` | Ready for RF-DETR small | `source.rtsp_url` | `output.insight.video_port: 9001`, `metadata_port: 9101` |
| `neat-tracking` | `examples/tracking/multi-stream-tracker` | `model.path: models/yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz`; set `inference.fps: 15` to leave MLA time for the others | one URL under `streams` | `output.insight.video_port_base: 9002`, `metadata_port_base: 9102` |
| `neat-pose` | `examples/pose-estimation/multi-stream-pose-estimator` | `model.path: models/yolo26m-pose-int8-b1.tar.gz` | one URL under `streams` | `output.insight.video_port_base: 9003`, `metadata_port_base: 9103` |
| `neat-drone` | `examples/tracking/yolo26-tiny-drone-tracker` | `model.path: models/yolo26n_p2_tiny_drone_int8_qat_b1_mpk.tar.gz` | one URL under `streams` | `output.insight.video_port_base: 9004`, `metadata_port_base: 9104` |
| `neat-blazepose` | `examples/pose-estimation/multi-stream-blazepose3d` | `models.detector_path: models/yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz`, `models.pose_path: models/blazepose_ghum_heavy_w16a16_mpk.tar.gz` | one entry under `streams` with `url`, `width`, `height`, and `insight_channel: 5` | `output.insight.video_port_base: 9000`, `metadata_port_base: 9100` |

Set `output.insight.host` in all six: `127.0.0.1` when Insight runs on the DevKit, otherwise the Insight host's address. The config is copied into the image, so after a config change run `build` and `deploy` again.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
Run these commands in the Neat SDK container, from `prebuilt-apps/`, not on the DevKit. `build` uses the SDK's Docker and container registry, and `deploy`, `dk container logs`, and `stop` reach the DevKit through `dk`.

Build the six ARM64 images and push them to the SDK's container registry:

```bash
${APP_DIR}/src/common/parallel-apps.sh build
```

Start the six containers on the DevKit, one after another:

```bash
${APP_DIR}/src/common/parallel-apps.sh deploy
```

To start only some of them, name them, for example `${APP_DIR}/src/common/parallel-apps.sh deploy neat-tracking neat-pose`.

Follow one application's log:

```bash
dk container logs neat-tracking --follow
```

Stop and remove the containers:

```bash
${APP_DIR}/src/common/parallel-apps.sh stop
```

`stop` sends SIGINT, which the applications handle as a clean shutdown.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
`dk container list` shows six running containers: `neat-segmentation`, `neat-detection`, `neat-tracking`, `neat-pose`, `neat-drone`, and `neat-blazepose`. Insight shows channels 0 to 5, each with video and overlays from a different application. Channel 5 also carries BlazePose's 3D skeleton for Insight's 3D Pose view.

The MLA runs one model at a time, so each application's frame rate depends on the combined model time of all six. RF-DETR is the heaviest and is the first to fall below its source rate. When the six sources together need more model time than the MLA has, the applications drop frames. Lower a source's frame rate or choose a smaller model in its config.

sections.title: Container Settings
sections.markdown:
`deploy` starts every container with the same settings:

- `--network host`: the applications use the DevKit's own network, so RTSP sources and Insight need no port mapping. Older DevKit kernels also lack NAT for Docker's default bridge network.
- `--user`: the DevKit user's user and group IDs. The accelerator and codec devices belong to its group, so the containers run without root.
- `--stop-signal SIGINT`: the applications shut down cleanly on SIGINT. As the container's main process, they ignore Docker's default SIGTERM.
- `--tmpfs /tmp`: Neat unpacks model packages here at startup.
- `--device`: the MLA, the computer vision unit, their memory heaps, and the video decoder and encoder.
- `--mount`: the DevKit's `/usr`, `/bin`, `/lib`, `/etc/alternatives`, and dynamic linker cache, read-only.

`src/common/Dockerfile` builds one image per container. It starts `FROM scratch` and copies only the example's binary (`src/cpp/pre-built` in the installed bundle, the build tree in a checkout), its `src/common` files, and the container's model folder. Because it runs no commands, it builds for ARM64 on any SDK host without emulation.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- If `build` reports a missing binary, run it from `prebuilt-apps/` after `sima-cli neat install apps`, or build the checkout as described in Development From Source. If it reports an empty model folder, download the model into `models/<container>/`.
- If a container exits at startup, read its log with `dk container logs <container>`. The application reports configuration and model errors the same way as a normal run.
- If every application exits with `closed owned platform capability unavailable`, the installed Core predates container support; update Core on the DevKit and in the SDK.
- If an application runs on the DevKit but fails to open the MLA in a container, update the DevKit with `sima-cli update`.
- If Insight runs inside the SDK on macOS and some channels stay blank, Docker Desktop is not forwarding all of Insight's UDP ports. Run Insight on the DevKit and set `output.insight.host: 127.0.0.1`.
- If an application fails to load a Neat library or reports a version mismatch, the DevKit's Core differs from the one the bundle was built against. Run `sima-cli neat install apps` again without `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES`.
- If two applications appear on one Insight channel, check that their configs use different Insight ports.

sections.markdown:

To modify, compile, or test this example, use the [Apps contributor workflow](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

`parallel-apps.sh` also runs from the root of an Apps checkout in the Neat SDK shell, using the binaries under `build/`. On a new SDK container, install Core before the first build:


sections.title: Concept

Finds faces in a folder of images with RetinaFace, then saves annotated results with confidence scores and five facial landmarks.

The application decodes the model output, removes weak and duplicate detections, and writes annotated images.

```bash
cd prebuilt-apps
```

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"

cd models
```

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/face-detector \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

### Python

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
The application prints one line per image with the number of faces found and the
file it wrote:

```text
[1/21] 000000081061.jpg: 0 detections -> 000000081061_retinaface.png
[2/21] 000000116439.jpg: 1 detections -> 000000116439_retinaface.png
[3/21] 000000129492.jpg: 2 detections -> 000000129492_retinaface.png
```

`io.output_dir` (default `sandbox/face-detector`) then holds one annotated PNG
per input image; with the packaged `assets/datasets/coco` folder that is 21
files. The C++ binary is much more verbose per image: alongside each of these it
prints `Model produced N tensor(s)`, a shape line per output tensor, a
`Detections: N` line, and a score and box line per detection. All of that is
normal; Python prints only the one line per image shown above.

Counts vary a lot between images. These are general COCO photographs rather than
a face dataset, and many contain no people, so `0 detections` on a given image is
normal. A run where every image reports `0 detections` is the case worth investigating;
`decode.confidence_threshold` is the usual cause. A wrong `model.path` does not
produce this — it stops the run outright, either reporting the missing file or
failing on the tensor count.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- Verify `model.path` if model loading fails.
- Lower `decode.confidence_threshold` if expected faces are missing.
- Adjust `decode.nms_iou` or `decode.top_k` if duplicate boxes remain.
- Confirm `io.output_dir` can be created.

apps.name: Single-Stream Thermal Face Detector
apps.summary: Detects faces and five facial landmarks in a live thermal RTSP stream with YOLOv5s-Face, then sends the overlay to Insight.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Detects faces and five facial landmarks in a live thermal RTSP stream with YOLOv5s-Face, then sends the overlay to Insight.

The pipeline keeps the video and landmarks on the same frame:

```
RTSP decode (NV12) --> branch --> video_sender (H264 RTP/UDP -> Insight)
                            \--> model (raw split heads) --> detections
```

Each frame sends one `pose-estimation` message with the left eye, right eye, nose tip, and both mouth corners. Insight draws them as labeled dots. The application sends one metadata type because Insight shows only one type per channel at a time.

YOLOv5s-Face returns raw box and landmark outputs. The C++ and Python applications decode those outputs with the same math before sending the five points to Insight.

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![Thermal face detector reference preview](./example-assets/face-detection/single-stream-thermal-face-detector/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- `sima-cli` ([documentation](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/sima-cli/))
  on the Modalix DevKit, or in a Neat SDK container paired with it.
- A running [Neat Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/)
  instance reachable from the target, with an RTSP source containing faces.
- The model expects an 800x800 compiled canvas; its on-device preprocess accepts
  NV12, BGR, RGB, I420, or grayscale input up to 4096x4096.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install on the Modalix DevKit, or under `/workspace` in a Neat SDK container paired with it. Only the example itself must run on the DevKit. If the Core and Insight selected by Apps are already installed, run the install as `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES=1 sima-cli neat install apps` to skip reinstalling them. See [Install Apps](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/README.md#install-apps).

Install the latest Neat Apps runtime and enter the installed bundle:

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/face-detection/single-stream-thermal-face-detector
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
Primary model: `yolov5s_face_raw_split`

Model packages come from the Model Zoo release below, which can differ from the
installed platform version.

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
sima-cli download \
  "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolov5s_face_raw_split_mpk.tar.gz"
cd ..
```

The command stores the package under `models/`; set `model.path` to the
downloaded `yolov5s_face_raw_split_mpk.tar.gz` file.

sections.title: Prepare Insight
sections.markdown:
[Neat Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) can host an RTSP source, receive video from `VideoSender`, receive landmark metadata from `MetadataSender`, and show rendered overlays plus runtime metrics in the browser.

In the Neat Development Environment, install the sample video assets:

```bash
sima-cli install assets/multi-video-sources
```

This provides 720p and 480p videos that Insight can stream as RTSP sources. This
example expects faces in frame, so upload a thermal or visible-light face clip of
your own when the sample videos do not contain any.

To create a reproducible RTSP input:
1. Run `neat` in the Neat Development Environment and open the reported `Insight Web UI`.
2. In Insight, open `RTSP Source`.
3. Use a sample video or upload your own video.
4. Start the stream and copy the RTSP URL.
5. Put that RTSP URL into `source.rtsp_url`.

Use the same `neat` output to set `output.insight.host`, `video_port`, and `metadata_port` from the reported `videoUDP` and `metadataUDP` ranges.

**Ports when the app runs on a board.** Insight runs inside the SDK container and
builds its URLs from the container's own view, so the RTSP link copied from the UI
carries the container-internal port (`8554`). An app running on a DevKit is
outside that container and must use the SDK host IP plus the **published** host
port instead. Read the mapping from `exposedPorts` in `neat --json` and never
assume the defaults:

| Endpoint | Container port (shown in the UI) | Host port (use this from a board) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RTSP | 8554 | `rtsp.tcp` → `hostPortStart` |
| Video UDP | 9000 | `videoUDP` → `hostPortStart` |
| Metadata UDP | 9100 | `metadataUDP` → `hostPortStart` |

Keep video and metadata on the same channel (0).

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`. Set `model.path`, `source.rtsp_url`, and `output.insight.host`. If Insight uses nondefault ports, also set the video and metadata ports reported by `neat --json`.

Keep video and metadata on the same Insight channel. The checked-in thresholds and runtime settings are ready to use for a first run.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
### C++
```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/single-stream-thermal-face-detector \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

### Python
```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

Open the Insight video viewer for the channel (e.g. `/api/viewer-url?src=0`) to
watch the annotated stream.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
This application writes nothing to disk; its output is the Insight video channel
plus the landmark metadata channel. It prints the resolved source on startup and
a count when the frame limit is reached:

```text
rtsp=rtsp://<host>:<port>/<stream> stream=1280x720@30 insight=<insight-host> video=9000 metadata=9100 channel=0
processed=200 video_sender=<insight-host>:9000
```

The packaged config ships `inference.frames: 0`, which runs continuously. The
closing `processed=` line prints only when a finite limit is reached, and
interrupting the run with Ctrl-C skips it in both implementations. For a bounded
check that ends by itself and prints the count, set a positive limit first:

```yaml
inference:
  frames: 200
```

Left at `0`, the live Insight stream is the success signal instead.

Either way, `processed` reports frames pushed through the pipeline, not faces
found, so a healthy count does not by itself confirm detections. Confirm those
in Insight, which draws the five landmarks as labeled dots on the stream.

The preview image is a reference visualization: it pairs the thermal stream
with its visible-light source and draws face, eye, and mouth boxes. The
application publishes only the five landmarks, not those boxes.

sections.title: Debugging Notes
sections.markdown:
Check the configuration before involving hardware. This validates and exits
without opening a stream:

```bash
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml --validate-config-only
```

- `source.rtsp_url must be set`, `model.path must be set` and
  `output.insight.host must be set` mean the value is empty or missing. Note that
  validation does not detect an unedited placeholder: the packaged
  `<rtsp-url>` and `<insight-host-ip>` are non-empty strings and pass, so a config
  you have not filled in still validates cleanly.
- `method SETUP failed: 461 Unsupported Transport` was observed once at startup
  against an Insight-hosted source, after which the pipeline built and the run
  completed normally. Treat a single occurrence as noise unless the pipeline also
  fails to start.
- If the run reports no frames at all, verify the RTSP URL from the board itself
  rather than from the machine running Insight. The URL Insight displays is not
  always reachable from the target, and the ports table above explains why.

- If the viewer shows video but no overlays, confirm `output.insight.host` and the
  metadata port are reachable and match the viewer's channel. Use Insight's
  `/api/ingest/stats` to check `metadata.messages_received`.
- If the streamed video looks blocky, raise `encoder.bitrate_kbps` in
  `build_pipeline` (the Neat default is 4000). Check the delivered rate with
  `/api/ingest/stats` -> `rtp.bitrate_bps`; the source stream itself is only
  re-encoded here, so a sharp source plus a blocky viewer means the encoder is
  starved.
- If the viewer shows no video, verify the video UDP port and that RTP is arriving
  (`/api/ingest/stats` -> `rtp.packets_received`, `media.seen_sps`).
- If keypoints look mis-anchored, the model may have been retrained with different
  anchors -- update `_STRIDES`/`_anchors()` in `src/python/main.py` and
  `kStrides`/`kAnchors` in `src/cpp/main.cpp` to match.
- Set `runtime.profile: true` to print rolling pull/decode/metadata timing and
  output FPS.
- Use `inference.min_score` and `inference.nms_iou` to tune detection sensitivity.

apps.summary: Finds SuperPoint feature points in a video and streams the annotated video to Insight.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown: Finds SuperPoint feature points in a video and streams the annotated video to Insight.

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![SuperPoint feature overlay](./example-assets/feature-extraction/superpoint-feature-extractor/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- `sima-cli` ([documentation](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/sima-cli/)) on the Modalix
  DevKit, or in a Neat SDK container paired with it.
- Neat Library with SuperPoint BoxDecode support.
- Insight or another RTP receiver for the annotated output stream.
- The SuperPoint model package installed below.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install on the Modalix DevKit, or under `/workspace` in a Neat SDK container paired with it. Only the example itself must run on the DevKit. If the Core and Insight selected by Apps are already installed, run the install as `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES=1 sima-cli neat install apps` to skip reinstalling them. See [Install Apps](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/README.md#install-apps).

Install the latest Neat Apps runtime and enter the installed bundle:

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/feature-extraction/superpoint-feature-extractor
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
| Model | Role | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `superpoint_mpk.tar.gz` | Default | Direct artifact |

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/superpoint_mpk.tar.gz"
cd ..
```

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`. Set `model.path`, `io.input`, and `output.insight.host`. Change the Insight port or channel only if your Insight setup uses different values.

Set `runtime.frames` to `0` to process the full video. The input must keep the same resolution for the whole run.

The included sequence comes from the TUM RGB-D visual-SLAM benchmark. Its camera motion and office
scene provide repeatable local features for SuperPoint to extract. The source, attribution, transformation, and CC BY 4.0 license are documented in
`assets/datasets/tum-rgbd/LICENSE.md`.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
### C++

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/superpoint-feature-extractor \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

### Python

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

Both implementations stream the overlay to Insight and print the number of processed frames,
average feature count, descriptor dimension, and selected video endpoint.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
This application writes nothing to disk; its output is the Insight stream plus a
single summary line printed when the frame limit is reached:

```text
frames=200 average_points=331.6 descriptor_dim=256 video_sender=<insight-host>:9000
```

`frames` should match `runtime.frames`, or the video length when it is `0`.
`descriptor_dim` should be `256`. For the packaged TUM RGB-D sequence
`average_points` runs in the low hundreds. An `average_points` near zero means
the pipeline ran but the model returned almost no features, which is worth
investigating even though the run exits successfully.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- Confirm `model.path` points to the qualified SuperPoint package.
- A missing or incompatible typed SuperPoint contract fails during model construction.
- Confirm the input is a stable-resolution BGR video supported by the target hardware.
- Confirm Insight is reachable at the configured host and UDP video port.
- Set `runtime.frames: 30` for a short smoke run.
