apps.name: Detection-to-VLM Assistant
apps.summary: Detects people in a live RTSP stream with YOLO26 and sends video to Insight. It can also crop the highest-confidence person and ask a configured vision-language model about them.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Detects people in a live RTSP stream with YOLO26 and sends video to Insight. It can also crop the highest-confidence person and ask a configured vision-language model about them.

The decoded frame branches inside a single graph to the detector, to the H.264 sender, and back to the application for the GenAI crop. Video and metadata therefore carry timestamps from the same frame, which is what lets Insight draw each detection on the frame it came from.

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![Detection-to-VLM assistant preview](./example-assets/genai/detection-to-vlm-assistant/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- `sima-cli` ([documentation](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/sima-cli/)) on the Modalix DevKit, or in a Neat SDK container paired with it.
- An RTSP source and an [Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) URL reachable from the target.
- The [LLiMa model manager](https://developer.sima.ai/software/genai-llima/runtime) available on the target when GenAI is enabled.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install on the Modalix DevKit, or under `/workspace` in a Neat SDK container paired with it. Run the `llima` commands and the example itself on the DevKit. If the Core and Insight selected by Apps are already installed, run the install as `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES=1 sima-cli neat install apps` to skip reinstalling them. See [Install Apps](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/README.md#install-apps).

Install the latest Neat Apps runtime and enter the installed bundle:

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/genai/detection-to-vlm-assistant
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
Supported detector packages:

| Model file | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `yolo26m-det-bf16-mla_tess-b1.tar.gz` | Default |
| `yolo26n-det-bf16-mla_tess-b1.tar.gz` | Supported |
| `yolo26s-det-bf16-mla_tess-b1.tar.gz` | Supported |
| `yolo26l-det-bf16-mla_tess-b1.tar.gz` | Supported |
| `yolo26x-det-bf16-mla_tess-b1.tar.gz` | Supported |
| `yolo26m-det-bf16-b1.tar.gz` | Supported |
| `yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz` | Supported |

Model packages come from the Model Zoo release below, which can differ from the installed platform version. Replace `<model-file>` with a file from the table.

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo26-detection/<model-file>"
cd ..
```

Set `model.path` to the downloaded detector package.

The default VLM is `Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-Autoround-a16w4`.

Search the supported models:

```bash
llima search
```

Install the default model:

```bash
llima pull Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-Autoround-a16w4
```

LLiMa stores models under `/media/nvme/llima/models/` by default. Set `LLIMA_MODELS_PATH` before `llima pull` to use another model directory, then update `genai_server.model.path` accordingly.

sections.title: Prepare Insight
sections.markdown:
[Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) can host the input stream and render the video and detection metadata. Install videos directly from the Insight catalog or through Insight's YouTube support.

In the Insight Web UI, start the required stream and copy its RTSP URL. Use the host and UDP port ranges reported by `neat` for the output settings. Use a host and published port that the target can reach, not `localhost` and not an address only Insight's own machine can resolve. Verify the URL from the target before running; the application prints the resolved source and its dimensions on startup.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`. Set the RTSP URL, detector model path, and Insight host and ports.

The packaged config sets `genai.enabled` to `true`. Check the server model name and path and update the prompts before using the VLM. Set it to `false` to run only detection and Insight output.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
Install the Python dependencies:

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
```

When GenAI is enabled, start the server in one terminal. The server uses port
`9998` and loads the VLM on the accelerator, as GenAI Studio does. If GenAI
Studio is running, for example after you set it up from Insight's GenAI tab,
stop it first with `run.sh stop` in its folder
(`~/prebuilt-apps/examples/genai/neat-genai-studio` when Insight installed it).

```bash
APP_DIR=examples/genai/detection-to-vlm-assistant
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/genai_server.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

Start the detection pipeline in another terminal:

```bash
APP_DIR=examples/genai/detection-to-vlm-assistant
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/detector_app.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

The GenAI path checks `/v1/models`, waits at least `genai.interval_seconds` between requests, and bounds queued and in-flight work with `genai.max_pending_requests`.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
Both lines below come from the **detector** terminal, not the server's. The
detector's startup banner reports the GenAI endpoint it will call, and it prints
each vision-language response as that response arrives:

```text
[genai-server] enabled model=Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-Autoround-a16w4 url=http://127.0.0.1:9998 interval=5s
[response #001] The person is seated and holding an object with both hands, appearing to rest or interact with it.
```

The server terminal prints its own lines instead, `added model: ...` followed by
`serving GenAI API on http://0.0.0.0:9998`; check there if the detector reports
the endpoint as unreachable.

Responses are deliberately infrequent. `genai.interval_seconds` sets the minimum
gap between requests, so at the default of `5` a short run produces only a
handful, and a response appears only when the detector has a person to crop. Few
responses is not a fault; none at all, on a source containing people, is.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- Verify the RTSP URL and Insight ports before investigating inference.
- Verify `model.path` points to the detector package.
- Verify the VLM server lists `genai_server.model.name` under `/v1/models`.
- If the GenAI server cannot start on port `9998`, another server already uses
  it, usually GenAI Studio. Stop GenAI Studio as described in [Run](#run).
- Disable GenAI to isolate the detector and Insight path.

sections.markdown:

- GenAI server: `src/python/genai_server.py`
- Shared runtime files: `src/common/`

apps.name: Neat GenAI Studio
apps.summary: Runs language, vision-language, and speech models on a Modalix device as the board-side backend for the GenAI tab in Neat Insight, with an OpenAI-compatible API.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Runs language, vision-language, and speech models on a Modalix device as the board-side backend for the GenAI tab in Neat Insight, with an OpenAI-compatible API.

The Studio has no user interface of its own. Insight's **GenAI** tab is the UI:
it relays every call to this backend, which listens on `https://<board-ip>:5000`.
The backend starts without a chat model loaded. Through Insight, or directly
through the API, you can:

- find compatible models already on the device, and download models from the supported Hugging Face accounts when the device is online
- load one language or vision-language model at a time without restarting
- chat with text and pictures, transcribe or translate speech with Whisper, and synthesize speech with the installed voices
- answer from local Markdown documents with RAG

Once set up, the Studio runs without internet access. The first `setup.sh` run and searching for or downloading a model from Hugging Face need it (see [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)).

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![Neat GenAI Studio preview](./example-assets/genai/neat-genai-studio/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- A Modalix DevKit with `sima-cli` ([documentation](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/sima-cli/)), the Neat Development Environment, and the Neat Library installed.
- The Neat Library's Python environment at `~/pyneat/bin/python`. If it is somewhere else, set `PYNEAT_PYTHON=/path/to/python-with-pyneat` before running the commands below.
- Neat Insight, to use the GenAI tab.
- Internet access on the board for the first `setup.sh` run and for Hugging Face downloads. Behind a firewall or proxy, allow `pypi.org` and `files.pythonhosted.org` (Python packages), `download.pytorch.org` (PyTorch for document search), `huggingface.co` and its download hosts (models and voices), `raw.githubusercontent.com` (English text-to-speech data for Piper, fetched with NLTK), and `docs.sima.ai` (Supertonic's compiled models, through `sima-cli`).

Run every command below in a shell on the board.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
If the Core and Insight selected by Apps are already installed, run the
install as `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES=1 sima-cli neat install apps` to
skip reinstalling them. See
[Install Apps](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/README.md#install-apps).

Install the Apps bundle, enter it, and name the Studio's directory:

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/genai/neat-genai-studio
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`. In a new shell, run the `cd`
and `APP_DIR=` lines again first.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
Install the Studio's environments, models, and voices once:

```bash
${APP_DIR}/setup.sh
```

`setup.sh` downloads the default speech-to-text model
(`simaai/whisper-small-a16w8`) from SiMa's [Speech & Audio collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/simaai/speech-and-audio-models), and the RAG embedding model
(`thenlper/gte-small`) into `/media/nvme/llima/models`, installs the
text-to-speech voices and the Supertonic engine, builds the default RAG
database, and writes `config.local.yaml`. When asked, pick the voice languages
to install. It finishes with `Install complete.`

No chat or vision-language model is installed by default; you load one from
Insight's GenAI tab (or the `/models` API) after startup. To download one during
setup instead:

```bash
CATALOG_MODEL_REPOS="simaai/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-Autoround-a16w4" ${APP_DIR}/setup.sh
```

On a board without NVMe storage, choose another directory for the models:

```bash
LLIMA_MODELS_PATH=/path/to/models \
SUPERTONIC_MODELS_ROOT=/path/to/models/supertonic-tts/models \
${APP_DIR}/setup.sh
```

Other `setup.sh` settings (environment variables; `${APP_DIR}/setup.sh --help`
lists them all):

- `CHAT_MODEL_REPO`: also download **and preload** one chat/VLM model at startup.
- `ASR_MODEL_REPO`: the speech-to-text model installed and made active at
  startup (set to `""` to install none). Setup checks the model loads and
  leaves it out of the startup configuration if the runtime refuses it.
- `ASR_CATALOG_MODEL_REPOS`: extra speech-to-text repos to switch between at runtime.
- `ALLOW_HUB_DOWNLOAD`, `HUB_ORGS`: allow Hugging Face downloads through the API
  (default `true`) and which accounts are searched (default
  `simaai TDoSiMa florianvoss`); a repo from another account is refused.
- `TTS_LANGUAGES`, `TTS_OPTIONAL_VOICES`: catalogued voice languages and optional
  voices (for example `mera`). Non-interactive setup installs
  `en,de,es,fr,it,ja,pt,vi,zh`.
- `INSTALL_SUPERTONIC`, `SUPERTONIC_MODELS_ROOT`, `SUPERTONIC_VENV`: the
  MLA-accelerated Supertonic 3 engine (default on), its model files (default
  `/media/nvme/supertonic-tts/models`) and its runtime venv (default
  `./.venv-supertonic`).
- `WEB_HOST`, `WEB_PORT`, `WEB_HTTPS`, `WEB_CORS_ORIGINS`: the backend's address
  and CORS allowlist written to `app.web`.
- `SETUP_RAG`: install document search ([RAG](#rag)), default `1`. On a board
  short on disk space or memory, `SETUP_RAG=0` skips CPU PyTorch, the RAG
  packages, the embedding model and the default database, and writes
  `app.rag.enabled: false`; everything else works as usual.

Re-running `setup.sh` (for example to add a model or voice) regenerates
`config.local.yaml` but keeps your `app.web` settings, the Supertonic paths and
whether RAG is installed (`app.rag.enabled`); the previous file is saved as
`config.local.yaml.bak`.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Most users change nothing. `setup.sh` writes `config.local.yaml` from the
packaged defaults in `src/common/config.yaml`, and any compatible model under
the model directory can be loaded without a restart. Edit `config.local.yaml`
only to change:

- `server.models.catalog_dir`: the directory scanned for models (default `/media/nvme/llima/models`).
- `server.models.chat`: chat or vision-language models to load at startup (none by default).
- `server.models.max_resident_chat_models`: how many chat or vision-language models stay loaded at once (default `1`; see [Keep several models loaded](#keep-several-models-loaded)).
- `server.models.asr`: the speech-to-text model active at startup (default `whisper-small-a16w8`).
- `server.hub.allow_download`: whether models may be downloaded from Hugging Face.
- `app.request.max_tokens`: the default response length for chat requests that do not set `max_tokens`.
- `app.rag.enabled`: retrieval-augmented search. Turning it on after a
  `SETUP_RAG=0` install needs the RAG packages: run
  `SETUP_RAG=1 ${APP_DIR}/setup.sh` instead.
- `app.web`: the backend's host, port (default `5000`), HTTPS setting, and
  `cors_origins` (see [CORS](#cors-for-other-browser-front-ends)).

Restart the Studio after editing the file.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
Start the Studio:

```bash
${APP_DIR}/run.sh
```

`run.sh` starts the model server (`${APP_DIR}/src/python/server/main.py`) and
the Studio backend (`${APP_DIR}/src/python/api/main.py`) as your user, without
sudo. The launcher restarts its workers after a model-load memory failure.
When startup finishes
it highlights **Open Neat Insight → GenAI**, prints the backend API address
(`https://<board-ip>:5000`), and keeps running
until you press `Ctrl+C`. If `setup.sh` has not been run yet, `run.sh` runs it
first.

Connect Insight:

1. Open Insight and select the **GenAI** tab. On the board itself Insight finds
   the backend at `https://127.0.0.1:5000`; from the Neat Development
   Environment it uses the paired DevKit. Otherwise enter the board address
   (`https://<board-ip>:5000`) in the tab's settings.
2. Load a model from the tab's model settings, or download one from Hugging
   Face there, then send a chat message.

Other commands:

```bash
${APP_DIR}/run.sh status   # running or not, and the backend address
${APP_DIR}/run.sh stop     # stop it from another shell (POST /shutdown does the same)
${APP_DIR}/run.sh --clean  # remove generated venvs, config, RAG db, voices and logs
```

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
- Once the backend is ready, `run.sh` prints `Neat GenAI Studio is ready.` and
  **Open Neat Insight → GenAI**, with the backend API address.
- `curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:5000/health` answers JSON with `"ok": true` once
  the model server is reachable, and lists the active speech-to-text model and
  the loaded text-to-speech engines.
- Insight's catalogue lists installed models, including one entry per DFlash
  or Gemma MTP target/draft package.
- After you load a model in Insight's GenAI tab, chat replies stream, Whisper
  transcribes recorded speech, and the selected TTS engine can read replies aloud.

To confirm the model server from a second shell on the board:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9998/v1/models | python3 -m json.tool
```

The output lists the speech-to-text model and any chat model you loaded.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- **The model server does not start:** confirm `pyneat` imports in the environment at `PYNEAT_PYTHON` (default `~/pyneat/bin/python`).
- **Insight cannot reach the backend:** check `${APP_DIR}/run.sh status`, then `curl -sk https://<board-ip>:5000/health` from the machine running Insight. The backend uses a self-signed certificate generated on first start; `NEAT_TLS_CERT` and `NEAT_TLS_KEY` select your own.
- **`setup.sh` says the runtime refuses the speech-to-text model:** check the model card's runtime requirements and update Neat or choose a compatible model from SiMa's Speech & Audio collection.
- **`setup.sh` stops on a download (connection refused, timeout, `429`):** `setup.sh` already retries Hugging Face rate limits, server errors and dropped connections a few times, so this is a lasting problem. Check that the board reaches the hosts listed in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites); behind a proxy, export `HTTPS_PROXY` first. Run `${APP_DIR}/setup.sh` again: files already downloaded and verified are kept.
- **A model download fails:** the message says why. For a model that needs approval, request access on Hugging Face and set `HF_TOKEN`; for a model Hugging Face renamed, download the new id it names.
- **A model runs out of memory while loading:** the launcher restarts Studio's workers to release model memory. The surviving API reports the failure; if it is killed too, Insight may report a lost connection instead. Choose a smaller model once Studio is ready; an on-demand load is not retried. Details are in the launcher output.
- **The launcher itself is killed:** start Studio again. Automatic recovery of the launcher requires external supervision configured by your administrator.
- **`/health` reports a voice engine with `"loaded": false`:** the engine failed to load (for example Supertonic while the accelerator was unavailable); the reason is `accelerator-unavailable` or `load-failed` and the details are in the Studio log. A speech request, or choosing the engine, retries it at most every 30 s.
- **Another instance is running:** `run.sh` refuses to start a second one; `${APP_DIR}/run.sh stop` stops it.
- **Start over:** `${APP_DIR}/run.sh --clean`, then `${APP_DIR}/setup.sh`. Downloaded models are kept; add `CLEAN_SUPERTONIC=1` to also remove the Supertonic model files.

sections.title: API
sections.markdown:
Everything is served on the backend port (HTTPS by default; set
`app.web.https: false` for plain HTTP behind another service). Any other path
answers 404. `GET /` describes the backend and `GET /health` reports readiness,
the API version Insight builds on (`api_version`), and optional features
(`features.rag`).

```text
GET  /health                       readiness: model server, active ASR model, loaded chat models, TTS engines
POST /v1/chat/completions          OpenAI chat (streaming), proxied to the loaded chat/VLM model; "neat_rag" adds document passages
POST /v1/audio/speech              text to speech (WAV)
GET  /v1/audio/voices              engines, voices and languages
POST /v1/audio/transcriptions      speech to text in the spoken language
POST /v1/audio/translations        speech to English text
     (the /audio/... paths without /v1 are the same routes)
GET  /models/status, /models/catalog, /models/card?name=, /models/logs, /models/logs/stream
POST /models/load, /models/unload, /models/asr, /models/delete            {"name": ...}
GET  /models/hub/search?q=, /models/hub/card?repoId=; POST /models/hub/download {"repoId": ...}
POST /benchmark/run, /benchmark/stop; GET /benchmark/status              TTFT / TPS benchmark
GET/POST /tts/engine; GET /supertonic/voices, /piperplus/voices, /voices; POST /supertonic/select, /piperplus/select, /voices/select
GET  /rag/status, /rag/inspect, /rag/search?query=...&k=3; POST /rag/upload (Markdown), /rag/reset, /rag/clear
GET  /board-camera/devices; /board-camera/snapshot?device=/dev/videoN   cameras on the board; a JPEG snapshot
POST /shutdown                     stop the Studio (not reachable cross-origin)
```

Quick checks from the board:

```bash
B=https://127.0.0.1:5000
curl -sk $B/health
curl -sk $B/models/status | python3 -m json.tool
curl -sk -X POST $B/models/load -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"<catalog-model-name>"}'
curl -sk -N $B/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"<catalog-model-name>","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello."}]}'
```

`src/python/api/apitest/audio_e2e.sh [host:port | base URL]` checks the workflow
end to end against a running backend: synthesized speech is transcribed back to
its words, German speech translates to English, the chat model answers, and,
when `/health` lists `features.rag`, document search returns passages and a
chat with `neat_rag` uses them, and the board camera lists its devices. With
`BOARD_CAMERA_DEVICE=/dev/videoN` set to a camera attached to the board, it
also checks that a snapshot returns a JPEG. It exits non-zero on any failure.
`src/python/api/apitest/backend_runtime_test.sh` exercises the model server and
the speech routes. The other scripts there (`speech.sh`, `transcriptions.sh`,
`translations.sh`, `chat.sh`, `completions.sh`) wrap single calls. They take a
full base URL (`http://…` when `app.web.https` is false) or `STUDIO_URL`.

### Models
`POST /models/load` loads a catalog model and warms it. `GET /models/logs/stream`
streams the load progress as server-sent events. If a load hits an accelerator
out-of-memory error, Studio returns HTTP 503 and restarts its backend to release
memory. Only configured startup models reload; the failed selection is not retried.

#### Keep several models loaded
By default one chat/VLM model is loaded at a time, and loading another replaces
it. To keep several loaded side by side, for example to compare them, raise
`server.models.max_resident_chat_models` in `config.local.yaml` (or set
`MAX_RESIDENT_CHAT_MODELS` before `setup.sh`), then restart the Studio. Each
loaded model answers on `/v1/chat/completions` under its own name, and clients
can use them at the same time. The Insight GenAI tab expects one loaded chat
model until it supports several, so keep the default for it.

Past the limit, the Studio never unloads a model on its own, because another
client may be using it. The load is refused with `409` and the loaded models,
and it succeeds once the request names the ones to unload:

```bash
curl -sk -X POST $B/models/load -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"<catalog-model-name>","unload":["<loaded-model-name>"]}'
```

`GET /models/status` lists the loaded models (`resident`, most recently loaded
first; loading a model that is loaded already moves it to the front) and the limit (`maxResident`). Each catalog entry reports the
ELF file bytes used to estimate load time (`acceleratorBytes`), the tokens it reads
at once (`contextTokens`), and its tokenizer (`tokenizerPath`). ELF size is not
resident memory usage. Target/draft packages appear as one model.

#### Limits and what the Studio does at them
Studio reports capacity and runtime failures through the model API.

| Situation | What the Studio does |
| --- | --- |
| **More models than the limit** | Refused before anything changes (`409`, `"code": "resident_limit"`, with `resident` and how many to unload in `needed`). |
| **Accelerator memory full**: a model that won't fit beside the loaded ones | HTTP 503, `"code": "out_of_memory"`, followed by a backend restart. Other accelerator load failures use `"code": "model_load_failed"` and require a manual restart. Running without `run.sh` also requires a manual restart. |
| **Storage full**: a download bigger than the free space | Refused before it starts, keeping 1 GB free for the board. A disk that fills during a download is reported as such. |
| **Prompt exceeds the context** | Core's `context_length_exceeded` error is passed through (HTTP 400, or an SSE error). Studio preserves the full history without token counting or automatic trimming. |
| **Generation reaches the context or output-token limit** | Core's `finish_reason: "length"` is passed through with the generated text. |
| **Accelerator busy** (Platform 3.0: `rc=-11`, kernel log `no free bank`, when several models run at once) | Retried once automatically, for streamed and whole replies, when no text had come back yet; otherwise the error is passed on. |

Speech-to-text has its own slot. `POST /models/asr` makes another ASR model
active (evicting the previous one) without touching the chat model. The switch
is not persistent: `server.models.asr` is what a restart re-selects. Set
`STUDIO_ASR_WARMUP=0` to skip the warm-up a switch performs.

`/models/hub/search` lists compatible models in the accounts in
`server.hub.orgs`, and `/models/hub/download` streams the download progress as
NDJSON. Downloads land under `catalog_dir`; a repo from an account other than
`simaai` is stored as `<org>@<name>`.

### Speech and transcription
```text
POST /v1/audio/speech            JSON
  input            required, up to 4096 characters
  model            default | supertonic | piper-plus | piper-tts   (a named engine is used or refused, never swapped;
                   OpenAI's tts-1 / tts-1-hd / gpt-4o-mini-tts mean default; any other name answers 400)
  voice            Supertonic speaker F1-F5 / M1-M5, per request. The Piper engines speak with the voice
                   selected for the language (POST /voices/select, /piperplus/select): omit voice or name
                   that one; any other Piper voice answers 400 rather than a different voice
  speed            0.25-4.0 (default 1.0); clamped to the engine's range, effective value in X-Speed
  response_format  wav (the only format produced; anything else answers 400)
  language         extension: ISO code the text is in (default en; auto means en)
  -> 200 audio/wav with X-Engine, X-Voice, X-Language, X-Speed, X-RTF, X-Audio-Duration, X-Elapsed-Time
     400 {error, param} | 503 {error, reason, engine} when the engine cannot serve the language

POST /v1/audio/transcriptions    multipart/form-data
  file             required (WAV, WebM/Opus, MP4/AAC, ... the server decodes with libavformat; up to 25 MiB)
  model            optional speech-to-text model; default: the active one
  language         optional ISO code or auto (default)
  response_format  json (default) -> {"text"} | verbose_json -> text plus language, language_detected,
                   tts_language, no_speech_prob, avg_logprob, ignored, reason, model | text -> text/plain
  -> headers X-ASR-Model, X-Elapsed-Time; 400 missing file | 413 too large | 503 no ASR active / server unreachable

POST /v1/audio/translations      multipart/form-data, same fields and limits as transcriptions
  -> the speech translated into English (Whisper's translate task); verbose_json adds
     task: "translate", language = the detected source language, tts_language: "en";
     headers X-ASR-Model, X-Task, X-Elapsed-Time

GET  /v1/audio/voices            extension: discovery
  -> {default_engine, languages, engines: [{key, label, loaded, languages, voices: [{id, label, ...}]}]}
```

`utterance_speed` / `utteranceSpeed` are still accepted on the speech route as
deprecated aliases of `speed`. In `verbose_json`, a recording is marked
`ignored` when `no_speech_prob > 0.6` or `avg_logprob <= -1.0`; override the
thresholds with `ASR_NO_SPEECH_THRESHOLD` and `ASR_LOGPROB_THRESHOLD` in the
environment of `run.sh`.

### Text-to-speech engines
| Engine | Licence | Runtime | Languages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Supertonic 3** | OpenRAIL model terms (see notices) | PyNeat on the **MLA** (vector field + vocoder), onnxruntime (CPU text front end) | 30+ incl. English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, **Korean**, Vietnamese (not Chinese) |
| **piper-plus** | MIT runtime; model-specific terms | onnxruntime (CPU) | Japanese, English, Chinese, Spanish, French, Portuguese |
| **piper-tts** | GPL-3.0 runtime; model-specific terms | onnxruntime (CPU) | English, Chinese, Spanish, French, Portuguese, German, Italian, Norwegian, Vietnamese |

- With `model: default`, a router picks the engine per language. The preferred
  engine is `supertonic` when its runtime loaded and `piper-tts` otherwise;
  `POST /tts/engine` changes the preference for languages more than one engine
  can speak.
- **Supertonic 3** runtime is vendored under `src/python/api/tts/supertonic_sima/`
  (see its README for provenance). It offers ten speakers (F1-F5, M1-M5).
  Each denoising step evaluates conditional and unconditional guidance together
  in one batch-two vector-estimator call; the vocoder remains batch one.
  `SUPERTONIC_VOICE` picks the startup speaker; `SUPERTONIC_STEPS` (5-12,
  default 8) trades quality for latency. It runs in its own venv
  (`./.venv-supertonic`, requirements in `src/python/requirements-supertonic.txt`
  plus the installed PyNeat) and worker process. `setup.sh` downloads its model
  files from [Supertone/supertonic-3](https://huggingface.co/Supertone/supertonic-3)
  and its runtime constants from
  [florianvoss/supertonic-3-sima](https://huggingface.co/florianvoss/supertonic-3-sima)
  at pinned revisions. Both compiled models come from the SiMa model zoo with
  `sima-cli download`; `src/python/api/tts/supertonic_sima/model_assets.json`
  records their addresses and checksums. Every file is
  verified by SHA-256, and each `setup.sh` run repairs missing or changed files.
  Supertonic needs Platform 3.0 or newer; when the runtime is missing the engine
  is not offered. The models root and venv are persisted under
  `app.tts.supertonic` in `config.local.yaml`.
- **CPU engines load on demand** when Supertonic is available; only languages
  Supertonic cannot speak (Chinese, Norwegian) get their Piper voice at startup.
- **piper-tts runs in its own venv** (`.venv-pipertts`) through a subprocess
  worker, because piper-tts and piper-plus both ship a top-level `piper`
  package. Its voices are split into encoder and decoder ONNX files during setup.
- **Japanese** defaults to Piper Plus CSS10; **MERA** is an optional Piper Plus
  model downloaded and verified when it is selected. **Chinese** defaults to the
  dedicated Huayan Piper voice. **Korean** needs Supertonic 3.
- The reviewed catalog is `src/python/api/tts/voice_catalog.json`: compact
  licence labels, pinned upstream revisions and SHA-256 checksums. Models under
  `CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0` are excluded. See
  [Third-party TTS models](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/examples/genai/neat-genai-studio/THIRD_PARTY_TTS_MODELS.md)
  for attribution notices.

### RAG
RAG is enabled by default after `setup.sh`, which builds
`src/python/api/milvus.db` (and `milvus.meta.json`) from the bundled
`src/common/rag/neat.md`. The backend starts the search service when the
database exists. A `SETUP_RAG=0` install leaves RAG off and the RAG requests
below answer 409; `SETUP_RAG=1 ${APP_DIR}/setup.sh` adds it later.

`POST /v1/chat/completions` answers from the documents when the request adds
`"neat_rag": true`, or `{"k": 5}` for the number of passages (1 to 10, default
3). The backend searches with the last user message, adds the matching passages
before it, and removes the field before the request reaches the model server.
The response headers `X-RAG-Hits` and `X-RAG-Sources` say which passages were
used. A request with `neat_rag` answers 409 when RAG is off or the documents
were cleared, 503 while the search service is starting, and 400 when the last
user message has no text. Every chat request is checked first: `messages` must
be a non-empty list of objects with a string `role` and a string or list
`content`; anything else answers 400 in the OpenAI error shape.

```bash
B=https://127.0.0.1:5000
curl -sk -F file=@/path/to/document.md $B/rag/upload   # replace the database with this document
curl -sk -X POST $B/rag/reset                           # back to the bundled document
curl -sk -X POST $B/rag/clear                           # remove all documents
curl -sk "$B/rag/inspect" | python3 -m json.tool        # what was ingested
```

`POST /rag/upload`, `/rag/reset` and `/rag/clear` answer `200` with
`text/plain` progress, one line per step; the last line starts with ✅ on
success or ❌ on failure, so check that line rather than the status code. They
answer JSON errors before the update starts: 409 while another update is
running or when RAG is off, 413 for a document larger than 10 MiB, and 400 for a
missing or non-Markdown file. An update replaces the whole database; if it
fails, or the client disconnects before it finishes, the previous database is
restored. `GET /rag/status` reports whether the search service is up
(`ok`, `starting`, `failed`, `no-database`, or `disabled`).

Passage text is added to the user's question, so the model follows any
instructions inside an uploaded document. Upload only documents you trust;
`/rag/upload` is reachable by any client that can reach the backend.

To use a different embedding model or disable RAG, edit `app.rag` in
`config.local.yaml`. To build the database from another Markdown file offline:

```bash
"${APP_DIR}/.venv/bin/python" "${APP_DIR}/src/python/rag/create_db.py" \
  --input /path/to/document.md \
  --output "${APP_DIR}/src/python/api/milvus.db" \
  --embedding-model "${LLIMA_MODELS_PATH:-/media/nvme/llima/models}/gte-small"
```

### CORS for other browser front ends
Insight relays every call, so it needs no CORS. Browser pages on other origins
that call the backend directly are refused by default; list the origins that
may call the API, or `*`:

```bash
BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS="https://insight.local:8443,http://10.0.0.5:3000" ${APP_DIR}/run.sh
```

To keep the allowlist across launches, set `app.web.cors_origins` in
`config.local.yaml` (a comma-separated string or a YAML list); the environment
variable overrides it for one run, and setting it empty turns CORS off for that
run. Allowed origins get CORS headers (the `X-*` timing and engine headers are
exposed) and preflight answers on the API paths; `/shutdown` never does.

### Update and clean up
To update, install the newer Apps release with `sima-cli neat install apps` and
run `${APP_DIR}/setup.sh` again. (`${APP_DIR}/run.sh update` refreshes a source
checkout or a single-example download instead; see Development From Source.)

`${APP_DIR}/run.sh --clean` stops a running instance, lists what it will remove
(the venvs, `config.local.yaml`, the RAG database, downloaded TTS voices,
`__pycache__`, the pid file and `*.log`) with the total size, and asks to
confirm (`-y` or `CLEAN_YES=1` skips the prompt). Downloaded chat/VLM/ASR models
under `catalog_dir` are kept.

Shutdown is graceful: both processes handle `SIGTERM`, so the model server
releases its models from the MLA and the backend stops the RAG worker (a
force-kill follows only after `SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 10).

### Manual Process Start
Use this only when you want two explicit terminals. `run.sh` also sets up the
text-to-speech workers, which this manual start does not.

Terminal 1, model server + control API (from `prebuilt-apps/`). The server runs
in the Neat environment, which may not have PyYAML, so give it a JSON copy of the
config made with the app's own venv, as `run.sh` does:

```bash
APP_DIR=examples/genai/neat-genai-studio
"${APP_DIR}/.venv/bin/python" -c 'import json, sys, yaml; json.dump(yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1])) or {}, open(sys.argv[2], "w"))' \
  "${APP_DIR}/config.local.yaml" "${APP_DIR}/.neat-genai-server-config.json"
~/pyneat/bin/python "${APP_DIR}/src/python/server/main.py" \
  --config "${APP_DIR}/.neat-genai-server-config.json"
```

Terminal 2, backend (from `prebuilt-apps/`):

```bash
APP_DIR=examples/genai/neat-genai-studio
"${APP_DIR}/.venv/bin/python" "${APP_DIR}/src/python/api/main.py" \
  --config "${APP_DIR}/config.local.yaml"
```

The model server's control API (`http://127.0.0.1:9997/control/status`,
`/control/load`, `/control/unload`, `/control/asr`) is local only; the backend's
`/models/*` routes proxy it.

See the Apps repository [contributor guide](https://github.com/sima-neat/apps/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for contribution requirements. The repository (not the installed bundle) also
carries the host-runnable unit suites under `tests/python/`, collected by

only pytest and PyYAML.

Outside the installed bundle, the Studio can also be fetched on its own with
`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sima-neat/apps/main/scripts/get-example.sh | bash -s -- neat-genai-studio`.
`${APP_DIR}/run.sh update` refreshes such a download, or runs `git pull` in a checkout;
`NEAT_APPS_BRANCH=<branch>` picks the branch and `UPDATE_DEPS=1` also refreshes
the Python environments.

The backend folder was called ui before it became `src/python/api/`. After
`run.sh update` from such a version, the next `run.sh` start moves the
installed voices, RAG database and uploads into `src/python/api/`.

Do not commit the generated `config.local.yaml`, `src/python/api/milvus.db`, or
`src/python/api/milvus.meta.json`.

apps.name: Multi Stream Multi Model
apps.summary: Runs a different model on each of up to four RTSP cameras in one process, and sends every camera's video and its own detection, segmentation, or pose metadata to Insight.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Runs a different model on each of up to four RTSP cameras in one process, and sends every camera's video and its own detection, segmentation, or pose metadata to Insight.

Each stream uses its own model and Insight channel. The default configuration runs
object detection, instance segmentation, pose estimation, and object detection on
streams 0–3. Source timestamps keep each overlay paired with its camera frame.

```text
Per stream: RTSP encoded ─┬─> codec passthrough ──────────────> Insight video
                          └─> decode NV12 ─> NV12 frame output ─┐
                                                                │
Application, per stream:  NV12 frame ───────────────────────────┘
                          └─> model graph (Preproc ─> inference ─> BoxDecode)
                              ─> boxes, masks or keypoints ────> Insight metadata
```

Every camera's receive-and-decode chain shares one graph and one run, because Neat
grants a decoder-admission lease only when a single graph holds more than one decoder.
Each model gets a graph and run of its own, so a stalled model cannot stop its
neighbours. The video the viewer sees is the camera's own encoded stream, passed
through untouched; Insight draws every overlay from the metadata.

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![Multi stream multi model preview](./example-assets/multi-model/multi-stream-multi-model/image.png)

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- `sima-cli` ([documentation](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/sima-cli/)) on a supported Modalix or DevKit target.
- Up to four RTSP sources, all H.264 or all H.265, and an [Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) host reachable from the target. Pointing several streams at the same camera is fine; each one still builds its own decode and its own model.
- Source frame rates that fit the decoder. Four 1920x1080@30 streams fit a DevKit; four 1920x1080@60 H.265 streams exceed decoder admission. Reduce the camera's frame rate or use fewer streams — the application does not resample, so `inference.fps` cannot work around this.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install the latest Neat Apps runtime and enter the installed bundle:

```bash
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/multi-model/multi-stream-multi-model
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
Model packages come from the Model Zoo release below, which can differ from the installed platform
version. Set each `streams[].model` to the matching package and keep the archives compressed.

| Stream | Task | Model package | Source | `decode` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Detection | `models/yolo_11s_mpk.tar.gz` | Direct artifact (Model Zoo `yolo_11s`) | `yolov8` |
| 1 | Segmentation | `models/yolo_11s_seg_mpk.tar.gz` | Direct artifact (Model Zoo `yolo_11s_seg`) | `yolov8` |
| 2 | Pose | `models/yolo26m-pose-int8-b1.tar.gz` | Direct artifact | `yolo26` |
| 3 | Detection | `models/yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz` | Direct artifact | `yolo26` |

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo_11s_mpk.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo_11s_seg_mpk.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo26-pose/yolo26m-pose-int8-b1.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo26-detection/yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz"
cd ..
```

These four packages are the tested set. The `decode` setting selects the package's head layout:
use `yolov8` for these YOLO11 packages and `yolo26` for these YOLO26 packages.

sections.title: Prepare Insight
sections.markdown:
[Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) can host the input streams and render
each output channel. Install videos directly from the Insight catalog or through Insight's YouTube
support.

In the Insight Web UI, start the four required streams and copy their RTSP URLs into `streams`. Use
a host and published port that the target can reach, not `localhost` and not an address only
Insight's own machine can resolve. Verify each URL from the target before running; the application
prints the resolved source and its dimensions for every stream on startup.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml` and set:

- `streams[].url` — the RTSP URL for each camera.
- `streams[].task` — `detection`, `segmentation`, or `pose`.
- `streams[].decode` — `yolov8` or `yolo26`, matching the package's head layout.
- `streams[].model` — the downloaded package for that stream.
- `input.codec` — `h264` or `h265`. All streams share this one setting, so every camera must use
  the same codec.
- `input.tcp` — `true` to receive RTSP over TCP, `false` for UDP.
- `output.insight.host` — the host running Insight.
- `output.insight.video_port_base` and `output.insight.metadata_port_base` — the first Insight
  port for each kind of output (defaults `9000` and `9100`).

`inference.fps` must remain `0`: this application uses each camera's source frame
rate. Configure a lower rate at the camera or RTSP streamer when needed.

Drop stream entries to run fewer than four models; the example accepts one to four. Stream *i*
publishes video on `output.insight.video_port_base + i` and metadata on
`output.insight.metadata_port_base + i`.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
### C++

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/multi-stream-multi-model \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

### Python

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

Both implementations read the same config and accept `--validate-config-only` to check it without
touching the cameras.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
Each stream prints its resolved task, model, camera, and Insight ports at startup:

```text
[stream 0] task=detection decode=yolov8 model=yolo_11s_mpk.tar.gz rtsp=<url> stream=1920x1080@30 insight=<host> video=9000 metadata=9100
[stream 1] task=segmentation decode=yolov8 model=yolo_11s_seg_mpk.tar.gz rtsp=<url> stream=1920x1080@30 insight=<host> video=9001 metadata=9101
[stream 2] task=pose decode=yolo26 model=yolo26m-pose-int8-b1.tar.gz rtsp=<url> stream=1920x1080@30 insight=<host> video=9002 metadata=9102
[stream 3] task=detection decode=yolo26 model=yolo26m-det-int8-b1.tar.gz rtsp=<url> stream=1920x1080@30 insight=<host> video=9003 metadata=9103
```

When the run ends (Ctrl-C, or `inference.frames` reached), each stream reports what it published:

```text
[stream 0] task=detection processed=1229 dropped_objects=0
[stream 1] task=segmentation processed=1210 dropped_segments=0
[stream 2] task=pose processed=1203 dropped_poses=0
[stream 3] task=detection processed=1205 dropped_objects=0
```

Open the Insight Video Viewer and select the four channels. Open a viewer tab for **every**
channel you want to see: Insight only forwards frames to channels with a viewer attached, and a
channel with no tab open renders nothing and correlates no metadata. Each one shows its own camera with the
overlay its task publishes: boxes on the detection channels, masks on the segmentation channel, and
skeletons on the pose channel. Insight draws these from the metadata, so the video itself is the
untouched camera stream.

Setting `output.debug_dir` and `output.save_every` also writes annotated JPEGs named
`stream_<i>_frame_<n>.jpg`, which is the quickest way to confirm a stream's model without a browser.

With `runtime.profile: true`, the packaged default, the application also prints each pipeline and
its element counters (`Pipeline:`, `ElementFlow:`, `Backend:`), and each stream reports its
throughput every 100 frames:

```text
[profile stream=1 task=segmentation] frames=100 output_fps=30.3 avg_result_pull_ms=24.3 avg_metadata_send_ms=4.1 avg_instances=3.7
```

Set `runtime.profile: false` for a quiet run.

With the four default packages and debug saving disabled, every stream tracks its source rate on a
Modalix DevKit: four 1920x1080@30 H.264 cameras each report close to 30 fps in `output_fps`, in both
implementations. This is the source rate, not a capacity measurement; the device has headroom these
packages do not use.

Setting `output.debug_dir` adds a host NV12-to-BGR conversion for every frame the application
pulls, not only for the frames `output.save_every` writes. Leave `debug_dir` unset for a
performance run.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- Boxes lag or lead the objects they describe: Insight is not matching metadata to video frames.
  Each message carries its source frame's timestamp and a frame ID (numbered per stream when the
  decoder supplies none); when the decoded camera frame has no PTS, the message is sent with
  timestamp `-1` and cannot be matched.
  Check `matched_video_first` in
  `curl -k https://<insight-host>:9900/api/ingest/stats` — it should track `messages_received`
  one-for-one. It also reads zero when two copies of the application publish to the same channel,
  so confirm only one is running.
- Boxes appear in roughly the right places but at the wrong sizes: `streams[].decode` does not match
  the package's head layout. Check it against the table above.
- One stream is silent while the others work: confirm that its camera URL plays and that its
  Insight metadata port is not taken by another application.
- A stream reports a nonzero `dropped_objects`, `dropped_segments` or `dropped_poses` at exit: a
  frame's results did not fit one metadata message, so the lowest-confidence ones were left out.
  Lower `inference.max_detections` or raise `inference.min_score`.
- The application exits with `consecutive decoded frames were unusable`: the decoder is not
  producing NV12 frames for that stream. Check that `input.codec` matches the camera.
- The application exits with a `source pull`, `model pull` or `model push failed` error: a camera,
  decoder or model stopped with the reason shown. Check that camera's URL and that model's package,
  then start the application again.
- One stream falls far behind the others while the rest hold the source rate: the MLA is
  oversubscribed. Four 1920x1080@30 streams fit the small INT8 defaults; heavier packages do not,
  and the shortfall concentrates on a single stream instead of spreading. Drop stream entries or
  return to the default packages.
- Every stream is slow, or a decoder fails to start: the source frame rates exceed decoder
  admission. Four 1920x1080@60 H.265 streams do not fit a DevKit. Lower the rate at the cameras or
  run fewer streams; the application cannot resample, so `inference.fps` is rejected rather than
  silently dropping frames.

apps.name: High-Density Multi-Stream Object Detector
apps.summary: Runs one YOLO26 detector across 20, 30, or 60 RTSP streams and sends synchronized video and detection metadata to Insight.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Runs one YOLO26 detector across 20, 30, or 60 RTSP streams and sends synchronized video and detection metadata to Insight.

Unlike the general multi-stream detector, this application tunes the pipeline for high stream counts.

Each RTSP source is depacketized once, then Core fuses two branches into the same source pipeline:

```text
RTSP H.264/H.265
  ├─ latest encoded edge ─> VideoSender ─> Insight video channel N
  └─ decode ─> shared YOLO26 detector ─> timestamped metadata ─> channel N
```

The application expresses this fan-out with ordinary `Graph::connect()` and starts it with ordinary `Graph::build()`. Core fuses the eligible topology internally. `VideoSender` consumes the read-only encoded access unit before the decoder, so the application does not open a second RTSP session, copy a decoded EV buffer, run an encoder, or shuttle encoded frames through appsink/appsrc. The UDP sender uses `async=false` so its sink cannot hold the shared live pipeline in `PAUSED` while waiting for preroll from every stream. The encoded edge uses `RealtimeLatestByStream`; a congested Insight channel can drop stale encoded work without blocking that stream's decoder branch.

Detection metadata includes the source `rtp_timestamp` and is sent with nonblocking UDP. A compatible Insight receiver holds complete encoded RTP frames for 400 ms and matches metadata to that source timestamp before WebRTC forwarding. Keep one active viewer while validating metadata, as described below.

The three checked-in profiles use the same application and model:

| Config | Streams | Source resolution and FPS | Target FPS per channel |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| `config.yaml` | 20 | 1280×720 at 30 or 29.97 FPS, detected from the source | Source rate |
| `config-30x720p20fps.yaml` | 30 | 1280×720 at 20 FPS | 20 FPS |
| `config-60x720p10fps.yaml` | 60 | 1280×720 at 10 FPS | 10 FPS |

The target rate applies to both Insight video and detection metadata after startup. Each profile needs about 600 aggregate FPS, and none is yet validated to sustain its target: a C++ run of the 30-stream profile measured 18.6 to 20.2 FPS per channel.

sections.markdown:

- 20, 30, or 60 H.264 or H.265 RTSP sources matching `input.codec` and the selected profile.
- For H.265, the computer running the Insight viewer must support hardware HEVC decoding; Chromium does not provide a software decoder fallback for WebRTC H.265.
- H.265 playback in Chrome on macOS renders, but is not stable. Chrome's WebRTC HEVC decoder can stop producing frames mid-stream and fall back to a null decoder that discards what follows, at which point the tile stalls until the viewer reconnects it.
- Constant source frame rate, 1280×720 resolution, no B-frames in the selected codec, and a short, regular IDR interval. The validated sources use one IDR per second.
- The `yolo26n-det-int8-b1.tar.gz` model pack.

The application starts all source graphs together. Start every RTSP publisher before starting the application.

sections.title: Prepare Insight
sections.markdown:
[Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) can host the input streams and render each output channel. Install videos directly from the Insight catalog or through YouTube support. In the Insight Web UI, start the required streams and copy their RTSP URLs into `streams`. Use the host and UDP port ranges reported by `neat` for the output settings. Use a host and published port that the target can reach, not `localhost` and not an address only Insight's own machine can resolve. Verify the URL from the target before running; the application prints the resolved source and its dimensions on startup.

Verify each source before starting the application. A Modalix DevKit does not
ship `ffprobe`, so run this from the machine hosting the sources or from any
workstation with FFmpeg installed:

```bash
ffprobe -v error \
  -select_streams v:0 \
  -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height,avg_frame_rate,has_b_frames \
  -of default=noprint_wrappers=1 \
  <rtsp-url>
```

The result must report the codec selected by `input.codec`, `1280x720`, the selected profile FPS, and no B-frames. Using a different source FPS changes the output rate and is not the documented profile. The encoded Insight edge retains the latest complete access unit under congestion, so a one-second-or-shorter IDR interval bounds receiver recovery if an older access unit is replaced.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Choose one config under `${APP_DIR}/src/common/` and edit:

- `model.path`
- every entry under `streams`
- `output.insight.host`

Set `input.codec` to `h264`/`avc` or `h265`/`hevc`. H.264 is the default in all checked-in density profiles and remains the validated high-density configuration.

`inference.max_inflight_per_stream` and `inference.max_inflight_total` bound raw decoder-backed frames admitted to the shared detector. The 20- and 60-stream profiles use a total limit of eight; the 30-stream profile uses 30 so one aggregate frame interval can be admitted without an unbounded queue. The realtime mux retains only the latest pending frame for each stream.

Do not add the removed `inference.fan_in_policy` setting. Ordinary `connect()` and `build()` select the eligible realtime fan-in lowering automatically. The `runtime` settings (`profile`, `warmup_frames`, and the `*_detection_timeout_ms` deadlines) are still validated so existing configs keep loading, but they have no effect and the application prints a warning when they are present. The application publishes metadata from the first valid detection result and runs continuously until interrupted; warmup, throughput measurement, and progress deadlines belong to the E2E receiver. Video/metadata synchronization is performed by Insight from each payload's source RTP timestamp; there is no application-side video-delay setting.

The default 20-stream config uses `input.fps: 0` and enables probing, so the source determines its frame rate. Keep `input.width` and `input.height` matched to the source. The 30- and 60-stream profiles keep explicit FPS values and skip probing; their configured dimensions and frame rates must match the sources.

Insight channel and port mapping is deterministic:

```text
channel index: 0 .. stream_count - 1
video port:    9000 + channel index
metadata port: 9100 + channel index
```

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
Set the example and selected profile from the `prebuilt-apps/` root:

```bash
APP_DIR=examples/object-detection/high-density-multi-stream-object-detector
APP=./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/high-density-multi-stream-object-detector
CONFIG="$APP_DIR/src/common/config.yaml"
```

Use one of the named configs for the larger profiles:

```bash
CONFIG="$APP_DIR/src/common/config-30x720p20fps.yaml"
CONFIG="$APP_DIR/src/common/config-60x720p10fps.yaml"
```

Validate the selected config without starting RTSP or Insight:

```bash
"$APP" --config "$CONFIG" --validate-config-only
```

Run the C++ application:

```bash
"$APP" --config "$CONFIG"
```

Run the Python implementation with the same config:

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -r "$APP_DIR/src/python/requirements.txt"
python3 "$APP_DIR/src/python/main.py" --config "$CONFIG"
```

Stop the application with `Ctrl-C`.

Use one active Insight viewer while validating metadata. Insight currently has a single-viewer metadata rendering limitation; multiple simultaneous viewers can make box delivery appear intermittent even when the application is advancing normally.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
- Every configured Insight channel receives live video.
- Detection boxes appear on the matching channel.
- Video and metadata approach the source cadence for 20 streams, 20 FPS for 30 streams, or 10 FPS for 60 streams. See the profile table for the measured rate.
- Nonblocking metadata-send failures are reported as rate-limited warnings without stalling inference.
- `Ctrl-C` closes the graph and exits cleanly.

If channels do not start, confirm that every publisher was already reachable and that the configured source caps match the selected profile. Restart the application after restarting the publishers.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
Check the configuration before involving hardware. This validates and exits
without opening a stream or touching Insight:

```bash
"$APP" --config "$CONFIG" --validate-config-only
```

- `ModelPack: invalid_archive: archive path does not exist` at run time means
  `model.path` resolved from the config file rather than from `prebuilt-apps/`.
  Use the absolute path printed in Prepare the Model. Validation does not open
  the archive, so this appears only once the run starts.
- `output.insight.max_visible_streams cannot exceed stream count` means the
  profile's visible-stream count is higher than the number of entries under
  `streams`. Reduce it, or add the missing stream URLs.
- `failed to probe RTSP frame rate` from the C++ binary does not tell you which
  problem you have. The shipped profiles set `input.width` and `input.height` but
  leave `input.fps` at `0`, so the configured dimensions are used as-is and only
  the frame rate is probed. An unreachable source and a reachable source that
  advertises no frame rate both end at this same message. Confirm the URL is
  reachable from the board before assuming the latter, and set `input.fps` only
  once you have.
- The Python entrypoint does distinguish the two: an unreachable source raises
  `failed to open RTSP source for probing: <url>` before any dimension or rate
  check.
- Either way, verify the URL from the board itself rather than from the machine
  running Insight; the URL Insight displays is not always reachable from the
  target.

Runs YOLO26 oriented-box detection on up to four RTSP streams of top-down aerial video and sends each stream's video and rotated boxes to Insight.

An oriented bounding box (OBB) is a box that turns with the object. It fits ships,
planes, and vehicles seen from above, which an upright box would cover with

`src/common/dota_label.txt`, such as plane, ship, storage tank, and small vehicle.

sections.title: Prepare Insight
sections.markdown:
[Insight](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) can host the input streams and render each output channel. Install videos directly from the Insight catalog or through Insight's YouTube support.

In the Insight Web UI, start the required streams and copy their RTSP URLs into `streams`. Use the host and UDP port ranges reported by `neat` for the output settings. Use a host and published port that the target can reach, not `localhost` and not an address only Insight's own machine can resolve. Verify the URL from the target before running; the application prints the resolved source and its dimensions on startup.

sections.markdown:
Open `${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml`. Set `model.path`, add each RTSP URL under `streams`, and set the Insight host and starting video and metadata ports. Set `input.codec` to match the streams.

The checked-in inference limits are a safe starting point. Change them only when tuning throughput or latency.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
Validate the config without opening streams:

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/multi-stream-object-detector \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml \
  --validate-config-only
```

### C++

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/multi-stream-object-detector \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

### Python

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r ${APP_DIR}/src/python/requirements.txt
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml
```

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
The application prints one startup line per stream, then per-stream profile and
processed counts:

```text
[profile stream=2] frames=70 output_fps=20.364721259721044 avg_detection_pull_ms=0.43236884301794426 avg_metadata_send_ms=0.5690935856795737 avg_boxes=2.0
[stream 2] processed=200
```

The two implementations format these numbers differently: Python prints the full
float, the C++ binary prints at the default stream precision of six significant
digits. Compare the magnitudes rather than the digits.

The `[profile stream=N]` lines appear while the run is in progress, once
`runtime.warmup_frames` has passed, so they are visible without stopping the
application. Every configured stream should appear.

The `[stream N] processed=` summaries are printed at the end, and the packaged
config ships `inference.frames: 0`, which runs continuously. Unlike the
single-stream examples, both implementations here still print them on Ctrl-C. Set
a positive limit for a bounded check that ends by itself instead:

```yaml
inference:
  frames: 200
```

A stream stuck with no progress while others advance is worth investigating on
its own: verify that source independently before assuming a model or config
problem. To inspect results without Insight, set `output.debug_dir` to a
directory **and** `output.save_every` to a positive interval. Both are required:
the packaged config ships `save_every: 0`, which disables saving even when
`debug_dir` is set.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
- Replace all placeholder stream URLs and the Insight host before running.
- The application supports up to four active streams.
- Set either inflight limit to `-1` to use the Core default.
- Verify host and UDP port ranges if Insight receives no output.
- Use `output.debug_dir`, `output.save_every`, and profiling output for diagnosis.

Batch visual inspection of printed circuit boards with a custom-trained YOLO26n
detector. Every image in a folder is run on the MLA and saved back annotated with
defect boxes and labels.

Images of any resolution up to the configured capacity are accepted and may be mixed in one folder. Core
letterboxes each one to the model input on device, so boxes are drawn on the
full-resolution source image.

Six manufacturing defect classes are detected:

```text
missing_hole, mouse_bite, open_circuit, short, spur, spurious_copper
```

sections.markdown:

- Confirm `io.input_dir` exists and contains `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, or `.bmp` files, and that `io.output_dir` is writable.

- Exit code 4 means one or more images could not be read, or their annotated
  output could not be written; the run names them on stderr.

apps.name: PCIe High-Density Multi-Stream Object Detector
apps.summary: Runs YOLO26 object detection across many RTSP streams using a host and Modalix PCIe card, then sends synchronized results to Insight.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown: Runs YOLO26 object detection across many RTSP streams using a host and Modalix PCIe card, then sends synchronized results to Insight.

sections.title: Preview
sections.markdown: ![PCIe high-density detector preview](./example-assets/object-detection/pcie-high-density-multi-stream-object-detector/image.png)

sections.title: How It Works
sections.markdown:
The host receives each RTSP stream and sends the encoded video to both Insight and the card. The
card decodes the video, runs the shared model, and returns detections, which the host publishes to
Insight as metadata.

```text
Host machine                         Modalix PCIe Card
============                         ==================
N x RTSP/H.264  -- encoded video --> N decoders
  +--> Insight video                 --> shared model
                                      --> box decode/NMS
Insight metadata <-- BBOX results -- neatpciesink
```

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.markdown:
- An x86-64 Ubuntu host with the
  [SiMa.ai PCIe driver](https://developer.sima.ai/hardware/getting-started/pcie-mode/driver-installation)
  and matching Neat PCIe host development package.
- A Modalix PCIe Card with a matching Neat Core installation.
- Passwordless SSH access to the card using `~/.ssh/sima_neat_pcie_ed25519`.
- 20, 30, or 60 H.264 RTSP sources and an Insight instance reachable from the host.
- A source checkout of this Apps repository on the host.

sections.title: Install Apps
sections.markdown:
Install the precompiled card application on the Modalix PCIe Card:

```bash
cd "$HOME"
sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/object-detection/pcie-high-density-multi-stream-object-detector
```

The card binary is installed at
`${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/pcie-high-density-multi-stream-object-detector`.

To build the card application yourself, see
[Development From Source](#development-from-source).

sections.title: Prepare the Model
sections.markdown:
Download the model on the Modalix PCIe Card:

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p /workspace/models
cd /workspace/models
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/yolo26-detection/yolo26n-det-int8-b1.tar.gz"
```

Use this absolute path for `model.path` in the configuration:

```text
/workspace/models/yolo26n-det-int8-b1.tar.gz
```

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
On the host, copy the profile closest to the intended workload:

| Profile | Streams | Input |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `config.yaml` | 20 | 1280x720 at 30 FPS |
| `config-30x720p20fps.yaml` | 30 | 1280x720 at 20 FPS |
| `config-60x720p10fps.yaml` | 60 | 1280x720 at 10 FPS |

```bash
APP_DIR=examples/object-detection/pcie-high-density-multi-stream-object-detector
cp "$APP_DIR/src/common/config-60x720p10fps.yaml" "$APP_DIR/src/common/config.local.yaml"
```

Edit `config.local.yaml` and set:

- `model.path` to the absolute model path on the card.
- `streams` to exactly 20, 30, or 60 RTSP URLs.
- `output.insight.host` to the Insight address.
- `card.card_id` and `card.queue` if their defaults are not appropriate.

The supplied profiles start RTSP streams 50 ms apart to avoid a simultaneous decoder startup
burst. Set `input.startup_stagger_ms` to `0` to disable the ramp.

The launcher copies this configuration to the card automatically.

sections.title: Build the Host Application
sections.markdown:
The host application is not precompiled. Install the PCIe host package for the host OS:

```bash
# Ubuntu 22.04
sima-cli neat install core/pciehost/ubuntu22/amd64@v0.6.0

# Ubuntu 24.04
sima-cli neat install core/pciehost/ubuntu24/amd64@v0.6.0
```

Build the host application from the Apps repository root:

```bash
APP_DIR=examples/object-detection/pcie-high-density-multi-stream-object-detector
cmake -S "$APP_DIR/src/host" -B build-host-pcie -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build-host-pcie --parallel
```

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
Start both applications from the host:

```bash
./${APP_DIR}/run.sh \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.local.yaml
```

The launcher uses the packaged card binary under
`${APP_DIR}/src/cpp/pre-built/pcie-high-density-multi-stream-object-detector`,
waits for the card graph, and then starts the locally built host application.

Press `Ctrl-C` once to stop the host first and the card second. Run `run.sh --help` for nondefault
SSH, binary, timeout, or runtime-directory options.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
- Every active stream continues producing results.
- Insight shows video and matching detections on the corresponding channels.
- The 60-stream, 10 FPS profile targets approximately 600 aggregate FPS after startup. This rate has not been measured on a PCIe card.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
The launcher retains the card log after shutdown. Inspect it from the host with:

```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/sima_neat_pcie_ed25519 sima@10.0.0.2 \
  tail -n 100 /home/sima/tmp/pcie-high-density/card.log
```

Do not restart only the host against an old card graph. Stop the launcher and start a new session.

### Stalls and unclean stops

The host application exits with an error when frames are still admitted but no result has
come back for `runtime.stall_timeout_ms` (default: twice `pcie.result_timeout_ms`). A stalled
card does not recover on its own: stop the launcher, then reboot the card before starting
another session. If the host's own teardown exceeds `runtime.teardown_timeout_ms`, it stops
waiting for the card and exits. Avoid pressing `Ctrl-C` a second time during shutdown: the host
runs in its own session and the launcher drops its signal handlers while waiting for it, so a
second interrupt terminates the launcher before it finishes stopping and cleaning up the card,
leaving the card in the unclean state described below (reboot required).

A card application that does not stop on `SIGINT` is killed. That can leave PCIe endpoint queue
state behind (`si_pep_get_rqe: No context created for Data work queue`,
`Ran out of output buffers` in the card `dmesg`), and later sessions may stall or crash the
card. The launcher records such a stop in `card.dirty` under the card runtime directory and
refuses to start until the card has been rebooted. Use `--allow-dirty-card` only for debugging.

If the card's kernel crashes, the host driver logs `SoC Kernel Crashed` and the
`veth-simaai` interface disappears; power-cycle the host to recover the card. The card keeps a
persistent journal, so the previous boot's kernel log is available afterwards:

```bash
ssh sima@<card-ethernet-address> journalctl -b -1 -k
```

### Card memory per profile

Each profile allocates decoder pools and PCIe receive pools from the card's CMA region
(`CmaTotal` in `/proc/meminfo`, 1.8 GB on the Modalix PCIe Card). Approximate steady-state
usage measured with `yolo26n-det-int8-b1`:

| Profile | CMA in use |
| --- | ---: |
| 20 x 720p30 | Not measured |
| 30 x 720p20 | Not measured |
| 60 x 720p10 | Not measured |

Lower `input.decoder_buffers` or `pcie.pool_size` if `CmaFree` on the card approaches zero.

sections.markdown:

To build the card application from source, run on the Modalix PCIe Card:

apps.name: RF-DETR Detection and Segmentation
apps.summary: Run RF-DETR detection or instance segmentation on one H.264, H.265, or MJPEG RTSP stream and view the result in Insight.
apps.model_label: RF-DETR Nano, Small, Medium, Large, or Segmentation Medium

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Run RF-DETR detection or instance segmentation on one H.264, H.265, or MJPEG RTSP stream and view the result in Insight.

The application decodes to NV12 once. A 4-frame queue replaces stale decoded frames when inference falls behind. EV74 converts, resizes, and normalizes admitted frames for the backbone. Host code selects the strongest proposals and passes their boxes and feature tensor to the transformer. Insight receives video and matching detection boxes or segmentation polygons.

The backbone output and transformer input each use a four-entry blocking queue to preserve completed backbone work. These capacities do not include buffers held by active stages.

MJPEG reserves 32 decoded buffers so decoding can continue while inference and preview retain frames. This is tested headroom for the application, not an exact count of graph-held buffers. The raw NV12 storage is about 44 MB at 720p, 100 MB at 1080p, or 398 MB at 4K, before alignment.

TCP sources use RTP timestamps directly to avoid arrival-time corrections during high-rate replay. H.264 and H.265 video reach Insight as encoded passthrough. MJPEG video is re-encoded to H.264 from the decoded frames; when the encoder falls behind, the preview keeps the newest frames and inference keeps the full input rate.

sections.markdown: ![RF-DETR detection and segmentation preview](./example-assets/object-detection/rfdetr-detection-segmentation/image.jpg)

sections.markdown:

- An H.264, H.265, or MJPEG RTSP source and an [Insight endpoint](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/insight/) reachable from the target.

If the Core and Insight selected by Apps are already installed, run the install as `NEAT_APPS_SKIP_DEPENDENCIES=1 sima-cli neat install apps` to skip reinstalling them. sima-cli neat install apps
cd prebuilt-apps
APP_DIR=examples/object-detection/rfdetr-detection-segmentation
```

Run the remaining commands from `prebuilt-apps/`.

sections.markdown:
Prepare the model directory, then download the pair for your selected task:

```bash
export MODELZOO_VERSION="3.0.0"
mkdir -p models
cd models
```

For detection, set `VARIANT` to `nano`, `small`, `medium`, or `large`. Small is selected by default:

```bash
VARIANT=small
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/rf_detr_${VARIANT}_w8a8_w16a16_backbone_mpk.tar.gz"
sima-cli download "https://docs.sima.ai/pkg_downloads/SDK${MODELZOO_VERSION}/models/modalix/rf_detr_${VARIANT}_w8a8_w16a16_decoder_mpk.tar.gz"
```

```

Return to `prebuilt-apps/` after downloading your model pair:

```bash
cd ..
```

sections.title: Prepare an RTSP source
sections.markdown:
1. In Insight, open **Media Sources** and import a video from the catalog or your own file.
2. Assign the video under **Streaming Sources** and start the source.
3. Copy its RTSP URL into `source.rtsp_url` and set `source.codec` to match the video. Use a host and published port reachable from the target, not `localhost`.

sections.title: Configure
sections.markdown:
Edit `$APP_DIR/src/common/config.yaml`:

- Set `model.task` to `detection` or `segmentation`.
- For detection, set `model.detection.variant` to `nano`, `small`, `medium`, or `large`.
- Set `source.rtsp_url` and select `source.codec` as `h264`, `h265`, or `mjpeg`.
- Leave `source.width`, `height`, and `fps` at `0` to probe the stream. Width and height are fallbacks; a positive FPS overrides the detected value.
- Set `output.insight.host`, `video_port`, and `metadata_port` to the values reported by Insight.
- Keep `inference.frames: 0` to run continuously, or set a finite result count.

EV74 resizes the decoded frame to the input size required by the selected model.

Segmentation uses `inference.segmentation.mask_grid_size: 640` for smoother outlines. Set it to `108` for native contours with less CPU work, or `432` as an intermediate option. This only upsamples mask probabilities before contour extraction; the model output remains 108×108.

sections.title: Run
sections.markdown:
### C++

```bash
"$APP_DIR/src/cpp/pre-built/rfdetr-detection-segmentation" --config "$APP_DIR/src/common/config.yaml"
```

### Python

```bash
source ~/pyneat/bin/activate
pip install -r "$APP_DIR/src/python/requirements.txt"
python3 "$APP_DIR/src/python/main.py" --config "$APP_DIR/src/common/config.yaml"
```

Insight receives `object-detection` metadata for detection or `segmentation` polygon metadata for segmentation. Stop a continuous run with Ctrl-C.

sections.title: Expected Result
sections.markdown:
This application writes nothing to disk; its output is the Insight stream plus a
startup line and a closing summary:

```text
RF-DETR detection small h264: rtsp://<host>:<port>/<stream> (1280x720@30) -> Insight video=9000 metadata=9100
RF-DETR detection: completed=200 output_fps=30.8
```

The `output_fps` value above is Python's, which prints one decimal place. The
C++ binary prints the same line at the default stream precision, for example
`output_fps=30.7692`.

The startup line prints as soon as the source is probed, so it confirms the
task, variant, codec and resolution straight away. Check that probed resolution
matches the source you intended.

The packaged config ships `inference.frames: 0`, which runs continuously. Both
implementations handle `SIGINT`, so stopping with Ctrl-C still prints the closing
`completed=` line. Set a positive `inference.frames` if you want the run to end
on its own instead.

`completed` reports the frames processed, and `output_fps` should track the
source frame rate; a much lower `output_fps` means the pipeline is not keeping
up with the source.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.markdown:
Check the configuration before involving hardware. This validates and exits
without opening a stream:

```bash
python3 ${APP_DIR}/src/python/main.py \
  --config ${APP_DIR}/src/common/config.yaml --validate-config-only
```

A valid configuration prints, for example, `RF-DETR detection small
configuration is valid`. The C++ binary prints the same line without the variant,
as `RF-DETR detection configuration is valid`.

- `source.codec must be h264/avc, h265/hevc, or mjpeg` means `source.codec` names
  a codec this example does not decode. Set it to match the source.
- `model.task must be detection or segmentation` means `model.task` is not one
  of the supported tasks.
- A `model.detection.variant` with no model pair under `model.detection`, for
  example `xlarge`, fails with `xlarge must be a mapping` in Python and
  `model.detection.xlarge.backbone and transformer must be set` in C++.
- `model archive must use .tar.gz: None` means one half of the model pair was
  left blank in the config. Both `backbone` and `transformer` must name a
  downloaded archive for the selected task and variant. This is specific to the
  Python entrypoint, where a blank value becomes the literal string `None` and
  slips past validation, so the failure appears only once the run starts. The
  C++ binary rejects the same config during validation, naming the selected
  variant, for example
  `model.detection.small.backbone and transformer must be set`.
- `failed to resolve RTSP width, height, and FPS` means the source could not be
  probed, usually because the URL is not reachable from the board. Verify it from
  the board itself; the URL Insight displays is not always reachable from the
  target. Where the source is reachable but does not report its properties, set
  `source.width`, `source.height` and `source.fps` as fallbacks.

apps.name: Single-Stream Object Detector
apps.summary: Detects objects in one RTSP or MJPEG stream with YOLO26 and sends synchronized H.264 video and detection metadata to Insight.

sections.title: Concept
sections.markdown:
Detects objects in one RTSP or MJPEG stream with YOLO26 and sends synchronized H.264 video and detection metadata to Insight.

The decoded frame branches inside a single graph to the detector and to the H.264 sender. Both outputs therefore carry timestamps from the same frame, which is what lets Insight draw each detection on the frame it came from. Setting `output.save_dir` adds a third branch that returns the decoded frame to the application so it can write annotated JPEGs.
